Frequently Asked Questions

Can Halo Support Help Me with My Halo 5: Guardians REQ Packs?

Halo Support is happy to accept bug reports related to the Halo 5: Guardians REQ System and report those bugs to the development team, but we cannot fix issues related to redeeming REQ packs in Halo 5: Guardians. For help with REQ pack redemption issues, please create a ticket with Xbox Support.

Can Halo Support Help Me with My Promo Code?

All support for promotional codes is provided by the partner company for the associated product. For example, if the code came with a Monster energy drink, then they would be the company to provide the support. Halo Support does not have the ability to provide replacement codes or resolve issues with redeeming them.

The one exception to this is if the code itself will not redeem on Halo Waypoint because it does not have the correct formatting (incorrect number of characters or invalid characters). In that case, we can work to resolve the issue.

Promotional codes that unlock content in Halo games can be included with a wide variety of products like snacks, drinks, and toys.

Support for codes for a service, like an Xbox Game Pass 14-day trial are handled through Xbox Support.

Error Codes & Messages in Halo: Campaign Evolved

This article outlines various errors you may encounter in Halo: Campaign Evolved and provides troubleshooting steps to help resolve many of them.

If you are unable to resolve your issue on your own, submit a Halo Support ticket.

ERROR CODES

Some error codes include a phonetic alphabet word (for example, Alpha, Bravo, or Charlie) to identify the specific issue.

Use this word to locate the matching error and follow the recommended troubleshooting steps.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code ALPHA)

We couldn’t sign you in. Make sure you’re logged into your platform account and try again.

This issue can occur if Steam is not running or you are not signed in. Make sure Steam is open and that you are signed in to the account that owns Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code BRAVO)

Sign-in couldn’t be completed. Verify you’re using a valid, non-guest account and try again.

This will appear if you launch Halo: Campaign Evolved without being signed in to the correct account. Make sure your PlayStation™Network account is signed in and connected.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code CHARLIE)

We’re having trouble reaching our servers. Please try again in a few minutes.

This error is related to a network connection issue. Check your internet connection and restart your network hardware if needed. Wait a few minutes, then try signing in again.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code DELTA)

Sign-in couldn’t be completed. Please check your connection and try again.

This error is related to a network connection issue. Check your internet connection and restart your network hardware if needed. Wait a few minutes, then try signing in again.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code ECHO)

We’re having trouble reaching our servers. Please try again in a few minutes.

This error is related to a network connection issue. Check your internet connection and restart your network hardware if needed. Wait a few minutes, then try signing in again.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code FOXTROT)

We couldn’t set up your player profile. Please try again later or contact support.

Check your network connection, then try signing in again. If the issue persists, submit a Halo Support ticket.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code GOLF)

We’re having trouble reaching our servers. Please try again in a few minutes.

This is typically related to a Halo services issue. Wait a few minutes, then try again. If the issue persists, submit a Halo Support ticket.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code HOTEL)

Sign-in couldn’t be completed. Please try again later.

This is typically related to a Halo services issue. Wait a few minutes, then try again. If the issue persists, submit a Halo Support ticket.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code INDIA)

Your account does not have access to this service. Check your account status or contact support.

Your account may be restricted or may not have access to this content. To check your account’s enforcement status, visit enforcement.XBOX.com. Alternatively, submit a Halo Support ticket or contact XBOX Support for more information.

Failed To Link Account. Already Linked. (error code JULIETT)

This platform account is already linked to another profile. Unlink it first, or sign in with the linked profile.

This error occurs when you attempt to sign in or link a different Microsoft account than the one currently linked to your Steam or PlayStation™Network account. Sign in using the Microsoft account that is already linked, or contact Halo Support to request an account unlink. For more details, refer to Account Linking & Unlinking in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Failed To Link Account. Already Linked. (error code KILO)

Your player profile is already linked to another platform account. Unlink it first, or sign in with the linked account.

This error occurs when you try to sign in or link a Microsoft account to a different Steam or PlayStation™Network account than the one it is currently linked to. You can either link a different Microsoft account, or contact Halo Support to request an account unlink. For more details, refer to Account Linking & Unlinking in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Failed To Login To Platform (error code MIKE)

We couldn’t verify your XBOX account. Please try signing in again.

Your account may be restricted or may not have access to this content. To check your account’s XBOX enforcement status, visit enforcement.XBOX.com. visit enforcement.XBOX.com. Alternatively, submit a Halo Support ticket or contact XBOX Support for more information.

ERROR MESSAGES

You may encounter issues at various points in the game that do not include an error code. Below are some example messages you may see, along with troubleshooting steps to help resolve them.

Something went wrong. Please try again

If the issue persists, contact support.

Try signing in again. If the issue continues, note the time and any on-screen messages, then submit a Halo Support ticket.

User is offline - You appear to be offline

Check your internet connection and try again.

Check your device’s internet connection and ensure you are signed in to your platform, then try again.

Login To Steam Required

Please sign into Steam and relaunch the game.

This issue can occur if Steam is not running or you are not signed in. Make sure Steam is open and that you are signed in to the account that owns Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Failed to record information into system

Something went wrong saving your data. Please restart and try again.

This error occurs when the game cannot save data. Ensure you have a stable connection, then restart the game and try again.

Failed to link account

We couldn’t link your accounts. Please try again later.

This error can occur for several reasons, including an unstable connection during account linking or a Halo: Campaign Evolved service issue. Wait a few minutes, then try again. If the issue persists, submit a Halo Support ticket.

Failed To Link Account. Not Found

We couldn’t find the account you’re trying to link. Please verify your account and try again.

Make sure your account details are entered correctly, then try signing in again.

Failed To Link Account. Relink Failed

We couldn’t re-link your account. Please contact support for assistance.

You will need to contact Halo Support for help re-linking your account. submit a Halo Support ticket.

Invite Only Session

This Fireteam is not joinable, please request an Invite.

The Fireteam you are trying to join is set to invite-only. Ask a member of the Fireteam to send you an invite. For help with sending and receiving invites, refer to our Co-op in Halo: Campaign Evolved guide.

Session is full

Please try joining another Fireteam.

The Fireteam you are trying to join is at full capacity. Try joining a different Fireteam or wait for space in the Fireteam to become available.

Cross-play Status Conflict

Your account settings do not allow cross-platform play. Update your account settings and try again.

Your account’s cross-play setting does not allow this session. This most commonly occurs when cross-platform play is turned off in your XBOX account settings. Turn on cross-platform play in your account settings, then try again. For help managing your account settings, visit Manage XBOX online safety and privacy settings.

This may also be caused by the cross-play game setting being toggled off. To check your cross-play setting status:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Account.
  • Under the Account section at the top, ensure Cross-play is toggled on. A member of the Fireteam has cross-play disabled

One or more members of your fireteam have account settings that do not allow cross-platform play.

A member of your fireteam has cross-play turned off. This typically occurs when cross-platform play is turned off in XBOX account settings. That player must turn cross-play on, or join a fireteam on the same platform.

For more info on managing your account settings, visit Manage XBOX online safety and privacy settings.

Microsoft Account login failure

Additional sign-in is required. Make sure your account isn’t active on another device, then try again.

Ensure that your Microsoft account is not signed in on other devices, then try again.

Account is signed in elsewhere

Your account appears to be signed in on another device. Sign out there first, then try again.

This error can occur if Halo: Campaign Evolved is already running on another device or window while you are signed in. Close the game on any other devices or platforms, then try again.

Please note that players may need to wait up to 20 minutes before trying again after closing the game on other devices or platforms.

Failed due to timeout

Your sign-in session has expired. Please sign in again.

This error appears when the 15-minute window to link your account or complete sign-in has expired. For more information, refer to Account Linking & Unlinking in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Country Not Authorized

This service is not available in your region.

This error occurs when XBOX services aren’t available in your region. For more information on regional availability, visit XBOX Supported Countries & Regions.

Halo Campaign Evolved on PlayStation®5

This article covers many Halo: Campaign Evolved features and enhancements that utilize the unique features of PlayStation®5.

Native Development

Halo development and support on PlayStation® aligns with the same standards applied to XBOX and PC. Both the PlayStation®5 and PlayStation®5 Pro versions are developed for their respective hardware to take advantage of console-specific capabilities, with the PlayStation®5 Pro version specifically enhanced to take full advantage of its upgraded hardware, delivering improved performance, stability, and feature fidelity.

Graphics Modes

Halo: Campaign Evolved includes two graphics modes players can choose between:

  • Quality: Runs the game at a target of 30 frames per second, prioritizing higher visual fidelity and resolution.

  • Performance: Runs the game at a target of 60 frames per second, prioritizing smoother gameplay and increased responsiveness. To change your graphics mode:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Options button.

  • Select Video.

  • Navigate to the Graphics Mode dropdown.

  • Select your preferred option (Quality or Performance). Each console uses its own resolution targets and rendering methods to maintain consistent visual output for each graphics mode. For advanced technical details about graphics modes on PlayStation®5 and PlayStation®5 Pro, read our Graphics Modes Overview.

High Dynamic Range (HDR) Support

High Dynamic Range is supported on HDR‑compatible displays. When enabled, HDR provides improved contrast, brighter highlights, and a wider range of colors. HDR settings can be adjusted within the console system settings and the in‑game menus.

To calibrate HDR and other display options in-game:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Options button.
  • Select Video.
  • Select Screen Calibration. For assistance with enabling and adjusting HDR in the PlayStation®5 system settings, visit How to Enable HDR on a PS5 Console.

3D Audio

3D audio is available when using compatible audio hardware, providing spatial sound positioning during gameplay. This enables players to better perceive directional audio cues, such as enemy movement and environmental effects, contributing to situational awareness during gameplay.

For step-by-step activation instructions, see How to Set Up 3D Audio on PS5 Consoles.

Suspend & Resume

PlayStation®5 suspend and resume functionality is supported. When the console is placed into Rest Mode, gameplay is paused and preserved, so you can return to the same session when you launch the game again.

This also integrates with Activities, enabling faster access back into gameplay without needing to restart from a checkpoint.

Play While Downloading

Players can begin playing before the full game download is complete. Once the initial required data has been installed, the first three campaign missions are available to play while remaining content continues to download in the background. Certain features, such as Skulls or Co‑Op, remain unavailable until the full download is complete.

Full Controller Support

Full controller remapping and tuning options are available on PlayStation®5. Players can customize button mappings, adjust sensitivity, and configure joystick inversion settings to support comfort and accessibility preferences.

In addition to full control customization, the following controller features are supported:

DualSense Haptic Feedback

DualSense haptic feedback translates in-game vibration and trigger signals into force feedback that reflects weapons, damage, and player effects during gameplay. Players can adjust the overall intensity using the vibration strength slider in the controller settings.

DualSense Adaptive Trigger Effects

Adaptive trigger effects add resistance and contextual feedback to supported weapons and interactions. These effects can be enabled or disabled using the trigger tension toggle, allowing players to control how adaptive triggers behave during gameplay.

Controller Speaker Audio Events

Certain in-game audio cues are played through the DualSense built-in speaker. This provides localized audio feedback, helping players easily identify specific gameplay events without relying solely on the main audio output.

Controller Lighting

Controller light colors and patterns update in real time to reflect gameplay conditions, providing additional visual context alongside on-screen indicators.

Cross-Progression

Linking your Microsoft account to your PlayStation™ Network account during setup enables cross‑progression for Halo: Campaign Evolved. When you sign in on XBOX or PC using the same Microsoft account, your campaign progress is shared across platforms, allowing you to continue your campaign on any supported device with your progress preserved.

Once unlocked, the following progression will automatically unlock across synced platforms:

  • Missions and Rally Point unlocks

  • Skulls

  • Terminals

  • Trophies and Achievements The following progression does not synchronize across platforms:

  • Mid‑mission checkpoints

  • Exact player position

Cooperative Play

Split-screen

Halo: Campaign Evolved supports two‑player split-screen co‑op on PlayStation®5, allowing two players to experience the full campaign together on a single screen.

Online Cross-play Co-Op

Up to four players can join a Fireteam and play cooperatively through online multiplayer. Fireteams support cross-platform play, allowing players on XBOX, PC, and PlayStation®5 to play together.

PlayStation®5 Pro Enhancements

PlayStation®Spectral Super Resolution 2 (PSSR2)

PSSR2 image upscaling is integrated into Halo: Campaign Evolved on PlayStation®5 Pro consoles. PSSR2 is an improved image upscaling solution that replaces the Temporal Super Resolution upscaling used on the standard PlayStation®5 and other supported consoles.

Higher Fidelity

On PlayStation®5 Pro consoles, the Performance and Quality modes for Halo: Campaign Evolved support higher average target resolutions and higher maximum resolutions for graphics systems such as post-processing and dynamic resolution scaling compared to the standard PlayStation®5, helping the game maintain higher fidelity.

For more details about technical features such as dynamic resolution and graphics modes for Halo: Campaign Evolved on PlayStation®5, read our Graphics Modes Overview.

Halo Infinite Battle Pass & Free-to-Play FAQ

In this article:

  • Do I need to buy the Campaign to access multiplayer?
  • How do I redeem codes from promotional offers?
  • What is the Battle Pass?
  • What is a Premium Battle Pass?
  • Does the Battle Pass come with my game?
  • Do I need to pay for the Battle Pass to get rewards?
  • Does the Battle Pass in Halo Infinite ever expire?
  • What is the difference between an Operation and a Battle Pass?
  • How often does a new Battle Pass come out?
  • What do I unlock by making progress in the Battle Pass?
  • Do I need to make progress in the Battle Pass to unlock customizations?
  • Can I transfer my Battle Pass progress to a new account?
  • What are Spartan Points what are they used for?
  • What are Halo Credits and what are they used for?
  • Why don’t I see the Halo Credits I purchased when I go to the Shop?
  • What is the difference between the Battle Pass and the Shop?
  • How often do the items for sale in the Shop change?
  • What are XP Boosts and how do I use them?
  • What are Challenge Swaps and how do I use them?
  • How do I access my free 25 Battle Pass levels from the Premium Pass Bundle?
  • Can I upgrade from the Premium Battle Pass to the Premium Battle Pass Bundle at a later date?

Do I need to buy the Campaign to access multiplayer?

No, Halo Infinite’s multiplayer is free to download and play on both PC and Xbox consoles. You do not need to buy the Campaign to play Halo Infinite’s multiplayer or make progress on the Battle Pass.

How do I redeem codes from promotional offers?

  • Go to halowaypoint.com
  • Sign in with your Xbox account
    • Make sure you are signed into the correct account associated with the Gamertag you wish to receive the promotional offer
  • Select your user icon at the top of the screen
  • Select Redeem code
  • Enter your code and press redeem
    • Codes need to be entered in ALL CAPS and hyphens need to be included Once your code has been redeemed you will be able to see it in your redemption history. The promotional item will only be available for that gamertag. Your redemption history will show the 25 most recent codes.

What is the Battle Pass?

The Battle Pass is a feature that lets you earn customizations for your Spartan, vehicles, weapons, and more by completing in-game challenges during multiplayer gameplay. As you complete these challenges, you earn experience points toward your Battle Pass and level up through its tiers. When you hit a new tier on the Battle Pass, you unlock the corresponding reward.

You can check on your Battle Pass progress through the or by checking your Challenges tab from the main menu (R on a keyboard or Y on an Xbox controller).

Halo Support and Xbox Support can receive bug reports, but we cannot help players complete challenges or purchase items.

What is the Premium Battle Pass?

Premium Battle Pass unlocks all earnable reward tiers in the current Operation’s Battle Pass. Premium also unlocks Battle Passes from previous Operations and Seasons that are no longer active.

Does the Battle Pass come with my game?

All the reward tiers on the Battle Pass that are labeled Free can be acquired without spending any money. The rest of the items can be earned if the player pays for the Premium Battle Pass. Progress earned towards the Battle Pass is associated with the signed in Xbox account. Other Xbox accounts on the same device will not have access to the earned items.

Do I need to pay for the Battle Pass to get rewards?

Some rewards on the Battle Pass are free and everyone can unlock those rewards. Other rewards on the track require a Premium Battle Pass to be claimed. If you make progress with the standard Battle Pass and then purchase the Premium Battle Pass, you will unlock the items from the Premium Battle Pass track up to your current progress.

Does the Battle Pass in Halo Infinite ever expire?

No. All Battle Passes in Halo Infinite are permanently available. It’s important to note that upgrading to the Premium Battle Pass is needed to progress a Battle Pass after the corresponding Operation is no longer active. Operation progress is applied to whichever Battle Pass the player has selected as currently active in-game.

What is the difference between an Operation and a Battle Pass?

In-game Operations provide new events, new gameplay content, new customizations, and more. New Operations happen for free and do not rely on your Battle Pass progress. Each Operation has its own Battle Pass. Each Operation’s Battle Pass will continue to exist for players to return to and make progress on, no matter what the current Operation is.

How often does a new Battle Pass come out?

A new Battle Pass comes out with every Operation. Older Battle Passes will continue to exist for players to make progress on with a Premium Battle Pass even after the Operation changes.

What do I unlock by making progress in the Battle Pass?

Making progress in the Battle Pass unlocks a huge variety of customizations, including weapon and armor coatings, weapon appearances, armor parts, entire armor kits, vehicle coatings, personal AIs, action poses, nameplates, charms, and more. All these customizations can be applied in the Customize menu.

Do I need to make progress in the Battle Pass to unlock customizations?

The Battle Pass is not the only way to unlock customizations. In-game Multiplayer events some Campaign actions, legacy rewards, and the Shop also unlock customizations.

Can I transfer my Battle Pass progress to a new account?

No, Battle Pass progress is unique to the Xbox account that earns it and is not transferable. Halo Support and Xbox Support cannot grant Battle Pass progress.

What are Spartan Points and what are they used for?

Spartan Points are an in-game currency that players can use to purchase customizations in The Exchange. Spartan Points are earned via some Battle/Operation Pass tiers and through Daily Challenges.

What are Halo Credits and what are they used for?

Halo Credits are the in-game currency that players can use to purchase customizations in the Shop and unlock the paid track on the Battle Pass. Halo Credits are purchased by using real money in the Shop within Halo Infinite or via the Halo Waypoint website.

Why don’t I see the Halo Credits I purchased when I go to the Shop?

If Halo Credits were bought somewhere other than the in-game Shop menu of Halo Infinite, please fully restart the game to see your purchase. When you update your Halo Credits balance by restarting Halo Infinite, don’t use Quick Resume on Xbox consoles or suspend on PC. You will see the Xbox Game Studios and 343 Industries logo intros if you’ve fully restarted the game. This includes purchases through the Steam, the Microsoft Store apps or webpages.

Halo Credits will only appear on the specific Xbox account connected to the purchase and cannot be shared to other accounts from a main Family account.

The fastest and most seamless way to purchase Halo Credits is through the Shop menu in-game. This ensures the credits go to the account you’re currently using and are added immediately without restarting the game.

What is the difference between the Battle Pass and the Shop?

The Battle Pass is a track of rewards that players make progress on over time by playing multiplayer. As they make progress on the Battle Pass reward track, they unlock more items. Offers for sale in the Shop are unlocked immediately after purchase.

How often do the items for sale in the Shop change?

Some offers in the Shop change every Tuesday, while others change daily.

What are XP Boosts and how do I use them?

XP Boosts are a type of consumable item that helps player progress their Battle Pass more quickly. XP Boosts increase the amount of experience gained toward Battle Pass progress for a set amount of time. XP Boosts can be purchased on the Battle Pass menu or bought in the Shop and then activated from Battle Pass.

What are Challenge Swaps and how do I use them?

Challenge Swaps are a consumable item that allows the player to switch out a current Weekly Challenges for a random new one at the same difficulty. Progress on a current Challenge is lost if a Challenge Swap is used to get a new challenge. Challenge Swaps can be bought through the Battle Pass menu or purchased in the Shop and activated from the Challenges menu.

How do I redeem the 25 level Battle Pass boost from the Premium Pass Bundle?

If you purchased the Premium Pass Bundle, your 25 level boost to the Battle Pass comes in the form of 100 XP Grants. Navigate to the Battle Pass menu to redeem them from the Boosts sub-menu.

Can I upgrade from the Premium Battle Pass to the Premium Battle Pass Bundle at a later date?

You can only purchase the Premium Battle Pass once. If you have purchased the Premium Battle Pass, the Premium Battle Pass Bundle will no longer be available.

Please purchase items with care, refunds for purchases made with Credits (in-game currency) are not possible.

Halo Infinite Campaign Installation Changes FAQ

As mentioned in the Season 4: Infection Patch Notes, the underlying systems related to the installation of the Halo Infinite Campaign have been updated. This article will address questions players might have about how this changes access to the Halo Infinite Campaign.

What is the “Campaign Installation Change”?

Since launch in late 2021, the Halo Infinite Campaign and Multiplayer experiences shared many of the same files and systems. This has allowed for a smaller installation size since the game did not require a Campaign version and a Multiplayer version of each shared asset.

With the launch of Season 4 in June 2023, the Campaign and Multiplayer experiences will no longer share these assets. This change will increase the installation size of the entire Halo Infinite experience and it necessitates a loading screen between the Multiplayer and Campaign menus.

Why is this change being made?

Separating the shared assets between the Halo Infinite Campaign and Multiplayer experiences reduces the potential that a change in one experience would impact the other experience. In other words, developers working on future Multiplayer updates will be able to improve and adjust different aspects of Multiplayer while Campaign remains a consistent and stable experience for all players.

Is the Halo Infinite Campaign now a separate game in my library?

No, the Halo Infinite Campaign is still listed within the Play tab of the Halo Infinite main menu.

If the Halo Infinite Campaign is installed, selecting Campaign on the main menu will initiate a loading screen that leads to the Campaign menu. Similarly, selecting the Multiplayer button on the Campaign menu will prompt another loading screen that leads back to the Multiplayer menu. Players on PC may see Halo Infinite appear to close then relaunch during this process.

If the Halo Infinite Campaign is not installed, players will be prompted to purchase or install it.

Will the Campaign menu function the same way?

The Campaign menu will function almost identically to how it did before, with some minor changes. When loading into Campaign, players will see a loading screen prior to entering the Campaign menu. Players on PC may also see Halo Infinite close then quickly reopen during this process.

Due to the separation in shared files and systems, the Campaign menu now operates independently of the Multiplayer experience. This means that player customizations such as Emblems, Nameplates, and Spartans are no longer visible in the Fireteam menus.

How does this impact Fireteams who try to access Campaign?

Players are still able to create and invite players to a Fireteam for Network Co-Op, however, they will not be able to switch between the Campaign and Multiplayer menus together. Fireteams switching between the Multiplayer and Campaign menus will need to leave then re-form their Fireteam.

To create or join a Fireteam for a Network Co-op session, players must first load into the Campaign menu then invite others to join their Campaign-based Fireteam or join another player’s Campaign-based Fireteam. Similarly, a Fireteam that wants to switch from playing Campaign to playing Multiplayer must first load into the Multiplayer menu.

Will my Campaign progress be affected by this change?

No, any progress that players have made in Campaign will be unaffected by this change.

How long will it take to load between Multiplayer and Campaign?

Load times between the Multiplayer and Campaign menus will vary depending on different Xbox consoles and PC specifications. On average, the loading screen between Multiplayer and Campaign lasts for approximately 15 seconds.

After installing Halo Infinite or updating the graphics driver on PC, the first loading screen upon launching the game may take longer than normal. With this installation change, the longer initial loading screen will also extend to the first time players access Campaign after installing the game or updating their graphics driver. Players will not experience this longer loading screen on subsequent launches unless they update their PC graphics driver or if the game is uninstalled then reinstalled.

How does this impact settings, particularly those used in both Campaign and Multiplayer?

Settings shared between Halo Infinite Multiplayer and Campaign will maintain their selections when transitioning between the experiences.

The Settings menu itself will appear almost identical between Campaign and Multiplayer, however, there are a couple of minor functional differences:

  • The Visual Language option in the Accessibility tab is only available in Multiplayer’s Settings menu. Any changes to this option in Multiplayer will carry over to Campaign.
  • Some options which use sliders in Multiplayer may appear as dropdowns in Campaign. Additional differences between the Multiplayer and Campaign settings may be introduced as more updates are released for Halo Infinite Multiplayer.

One other notable difference is that the Manage Game menu is inaccessible in Campaign. The Manage Game menu must be accessed via the Control Panel menu in the Multiplayer experience. This menu is used to install or uninstall content such as Campaign, language packs, and the HD texture pack.

To access the Control Panel in Multiplayer, press the gear icon in the bottom right corner or use one of the following shortcuts:

  • Press Menu on an Xbox controller
  • Press ESC or F1 on keyboard

What is the installation size for Campaign?

With this change, installing the Halo Infinite Campaign will require the following approximate amount of disk space per platform:

  • PC: 32 GB
  • Xbox Series X: 34 GB
  • Xbox Series S: 26 GB
  • Xbox One X: 30 GB
  • Xbox One or Xbox One S: 23 GB

Halo Infinite Match XP in Custom Games FAQ

Table of Contents

  • What is Match XP?
  • Can I earn Match XP in Custom Games?
  • Can I earn Match XP in Customs Browser sessions?
  • Are all Custom Games eligible for Match XP?
  • How do I know if a match is eligible for Match XP?
  • How do I earn Match XP in Custom Games? And how much can I earn?
  • Can I earn XP from joining in-progress Custom Games?
  • Is there a limit on how much Match XP I can earn in Custom Games?
  • What is the difference between Match XP and Carrer Rank XP?

What is Match XP?

Match XP is one of the progression systems used to complete seasonal Battle Passes and Operation Passes in Halo Infinite. Players earn Match XP for completing a matchmaking session and for specific accomplishments in that match, such as being on the winning team or being the match’s most valuable player.

The Match XP progression system does not include the Challenge system. Challenges can only be progressed and completed in Halo Infinite matchmaking. Additionally, Match XP does not progress a player’s Career Rank. Career Rank is progressed via Personal Score or Applied Score earned in matchmaking sessions.

Can I earn Match XP in Custom Games?

With the release of Halo Infinite Season 5: Reckoning, players can now earn Match XP by completing Custom Game sessions. Custom Games only provide Match XP for completing a match and not for accomplishments within the match.

Can I earn Match XP in Customs Browser sessions?

Yes, Match XP can be earned via Custom Game sessions listed in the Customs Browser menu. To learn more about the Customs Browser, visit our Halo Infinite Custom Game Browser (CGB) Overview article.

Are all Custom Games eligible for Match XP?

There are three eligibility requirements for Match XP in Custom Games:

  • Players must be in the Custom Game match for at least 3 full minutes. Completing a Custom Game with less than 3 minutes spent in the match will not award Match XP.
  • There must be at least 2 players in the Custom Game session for its entire duration. Custom Games that start with less than 2 players or sessions that drop below 2 active players will not be eligible for Match XP.
  • Players must complete the Custom Game session with a positive Personal Score. Players who leave before the match is complete or who complete the match with a negative Personal Score will not receive Match XP. This requirement is on a per-player basis, so players who meet this requirement will not be affected by other players leaving early or having a negative Personal Score.

How do I know if a match is eligible for Match XP?

When starting a Custom Game in Halo Infinite, the session’s Match XP eligibility will be listed underneath the mode settings.

When creating a Custom Game, the session’s Match XP eligibility is listed beneath the mode’s details.

When joining a Custom Game in Halo Infinite, the session’s Match XP eligibility will be listed below the map’s description in the Details menu.

How do I earn Match XP in Custom Games? And how much can I earn?

Match XP is awarded at the end of an eligible Custom Game. Once a Custom Game is completed, a Match Rewards menu will appear prior to the Post-Game Carnage Report (PGCR) to show how much Match XP was awarded.

Players will receive 10 XP per full minute spent in the Custom Game. For example, a player who spent 4 minutes in an eligible Custom Game will receive 40 XP, but a player who spent 3 minutes and 45 seconds in a match will receive 30 XP.

Each match is limited to 120 XP, meaning sessions lasting longer than 12 minutes will not award additional XP. Additionally, there is a limit of 7500 XP from Custom Game sessions per day.

Can I earn XP from joining in-progress Custom Games?

If the match meets the Match XP eligibility requirements, players will earn Match XP from joining and completing in-progress Custom Games. The amount of XP earned from joining in-progress Custom Games will align with the amount of time you spent in the match, not the total duration of the full Custom Game.

Is there a limit on how much Match XP I can earn in Custom Games?

Each Custom Game session is limited to 120 XP, meaning sessions lasting longer than 12 minutes will not award additional XP. Additionally, there is a daily limit of 7500 XP from Custom Games. This cap resets daily at 10:00am Pacific Standard Time (PST) or at 11:00am Pacific Daylight Time (PDT).

What is the difference between Match XP and Career Rank XP?

Match XP is earned by completing a matchmaking session and for specific accomplishments in that match, such as being on the winning team or being the match’s most valuable player. Match XP contributes to your Battle Pass progression.

Personal Score or Applied Score is based on how well an individual player performs during a match. This score, also known as the Career Rank XP, contributes to your Career Rank progression.

Learn more about Career Rank in the Halo Infinite Season 4: Infection – Patch Notes article

Halo: Campaign Evolved Graphics Modes Overview

This article explains how graphics modes function on XBOX Series X|S, PlayStation®5, and PlayStation®5 Pro consoles. It also provides an overview of some of the technologies used in Halo: Campaign Evolved that support these modes.

Graphics Modes

Every console includes two graphics modes:

  • Quality: Runs the game at a target of 30 frames per second, prioritizing higher visual fidelity and resolution.
  • Performance: Runs the game at a target of 60 frames per second, prioritizing smoother gameplay and increased responsiveness.
How to Change Your Graphics Mode:
  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button on XBOX, or Options button on PlayStation®.
  • Select Video.
  • Navigate to the Graphics Mode dropdown.
  • Select your preferred option (Quality or Performance).

Graphics technology

Halo: Campaign Evolved uses several graphics technologies to support visual fidelity while maintaining the selected frame rate target.

Dynamic Resolution

All consoles utilize a Dynamic Resolution Scale (DRS). DRS is used to automatically adjust the game’s rendering resolution in real time to help maintain a stable frame rate.

When the system is under heavier load, such as during intense combat or large on-screen effects, the resolution may be temporarily lowered to help maintain the framerate target of 30 or 60 frames per second. When system demand decreases, such as entering a quieter area with fewer enemies on screen, the resolution scales back up to increase visual fidelity and provide the best possible image quality.

Upscaling Techniques

Upscaling techniques render the game at a lower internal resolution and then reconstruct the image into a higher resolution output. This reduces GPU workload to increase performance, while maintaining a sharp final image on your display.

Halo: Campaign Evolved uses different upscaling technologies depending on the console:

Temporal Super Resolution (TSR)

TSR is an upscaling technique that uses information from previous frames to improve image clarity, reduce aliasing, and preserve fine detail while the game is running at a lower native resolution. This allows the game to maintain its target frame rate while delivering a sharper and more stable image than standard upscaling methods.

PlayStation®Spectral Super Resolution 2 (PSSR2)

PSSR2 is a PlayStation®-optimized implementation of temporal image reconstruction technology designed for use on PlayStation®5 Pro hardware. Like TSR, this temporal approach improves system performance while maintaining image quality.

How Can I Beta Test New Halo Content with Halo Insider?

The Halo team is always looking for feedback on their games and services. By joining the Halo Insider program, players can be considered for early access play sessions with in-development Halo games and content. These playtest sessions are called “flights.”

These playtest sessions are invitation-only and have specific goals, which means not everyone can be selected for every flight. To increase your chances for selection, make sure your Halo Insider settings are complete and accurate.

If this all sounds like something you are interested in, then join the Halo Insider program.

How to Change Language Settings in Halo Infinite

Halo Infinite is available in English, Japanese, German, French, Spanish, Spanish (Mexico), Italian, Korean, Chinese (Traditional), Chinese (Simplified), Polish, Russian, Dutch and Portuguese (Brazil).

Audio language packs are available in English, Japanese, German, French, Spanish, Spanish (Mexico), Italian, Korean, Chinese (Traditional), Chinese (Simplified), and Portuguese (Brazil).

By default, all visual language options are available in Accessibility settings. To change audio language settings, language packs need to be downloaded.

Configure audio language settings on Xbox consoles, Xbox app, and Microsoft Store

To switch Halo Infinite’s audio language, install the preferred language pack in-game.

  • Launch Halo Infinite
  • Open the Control Panel
    • Press Menu on Xbox controller
    • Press ESC or F1 on keyboard
  • Open Manage Game
    • Press Y on a Xbox controller
    • Press R on a keyboard
  • Select the preferred language pack(s)
  • Select Apply
    • Language packs will start to download
  • Once the download is complete return to the Control Panel
  • Open Settings
  • Select Accessibility
  • Select visual or audio language and choose the preferred language setting
  • Restart Halo Infinite

Configure audio language settings on Steam

To change audio languages in Steam, swap the audio language in the Steam app. There is no in-game option or download.

  • Close Halo Infinite if it is running
  • Launch Steam
  • Select Library
  • Right click on Halo Infinite and select Properties
  • In the Properties pop-up window, select Language
  • Select the preferred language from the dropdown
  • Once an option is selected, the language pack will automatically download
  • Start Halo, the visual and audio language will be the same
To make the visual and audio language different
  • Open Settings
    • Press Menu on Xbox controller
    • Press ESC or F1 on keyboard
  • Select Accessibility
  • Select Visual language and choose your preferred language
  • Restart Halo Infinite

How to Get Support for an Issue with an In-Game Purchase or Code in Halo Infinite

If you cannot see recent purchases reflected in-game, please fully restart Halo Infinite. Completing a purchase outside of the in-game Shop while Halo Infinite is running may not result in the Halo Credits balance updating.

If you have a problem with a purchase or promotional code, please contact the support channel for the store where the purchase was made.

  • Financial transactions (not Halo Credits) in the Shop, please contact Microsoft Support.
    • Refunds are only possible for Halo Credit purchases.
    • Halo credits cannot be refunded once redeemed for any in-game item or battle pass.
  • Report bugs in the Shop, please contact Halo Support.
    • Bug reporting only, we cannot refund purchases, interact with your credits, or grant items.
  • Purchases from the Store on your Xbox console or the Xbox PC app, go to Xbox Support.
  • Steam purchases, go to Steam Support.
  • If you have a problem with a promotional code, contact that retailer or the manufacturer.

How to redeem codes from promotional offers

  • Go to halowaypoint.com
  • Sign in with your Xbox account
    • Make sure you are signed into the correct account associated with the Gamertag you wish to receive the promotional offer
  • Select your user icon
  • Select Redeem code
  • Enter your code and press redeem
    • Codes need to be entered in ALL CAPS and hyphens need to be included Once your code has been redeemed you will be able to see it in your redemption history. The promotional item will only be available for that gamertag. Your redemption history will show the 25 most recent codes.

How to see your Halo Credits if you did not purchase them in the shop

If Halo Credits were bought somewhere other than the in-game Shop menu of Halo Infinite, please fully restart the game to see your purchase. When you update your Halo Credits balance by restarting Halo Infinite, don’t use Quick Resume on Xbox consoles or suspend on PC. You will see the Xbox Game Studios and 343 Industries logo intros if you’ve fully restarted the game. This includes purchases through the Steam, the Microsoft Store apps or webpages.

Halo Credits will only appear on the specific Xbox account connected to the purchase and cannot be shared to other accounts from a main Family account.

The fastest and most seamless way to purchase Halo Credits is through the Shop menu in-game. This ensures the credits go to the account you’re currently using and are added immediately without restarting the game.

How to Install Halo Infinite on PC and Xbox Consoles

Halo Infinite multiplayer is free-to-play and available on PC and Xbox consoles.

  • On PC, it can be installed through the Xbox app or Steam.
  • On Xbox consoles, it can be installed through the Store or Game Pass app. You do not need an active Game Pass subscription to play Halo Infinite multiplayer online on any platform. It is free-to-play for anyone with a free Xbox account anywhere it is available.

The store listings for Multiplayer and Campaign for Halo Infinite are separate. The free multiplayer is named “Halo Infinite” and the paid campaign is called “Halo Infinite (Campaign).”

Choose one of the following methods to install Halo Infinite:

How to install on PC

MICROSOFT STORE AND XBOX APP

To ensure a more stable experience, check Halo Infinite’s minimum and recommended hardware specifications and make sure your PC graphics drivers are up to date.

To install Halo Infinite multiplayer for free on PC using the Xbox app:

  • Open the Xbox app for PC.
    • You can find and install the Xbox app by searching for “Xbox” in the Microsoft Store app included on all supported Windows PCs.
    • If you are not already logged in, log into your Xbox account by clicking on the icon in the shape of a person in the top right of the Xbox app, then select Sign in.
  • Search for “Halo Infinite” using the search bar in the top right of the Xbox app and select the free multiplayer game from the search results, or use this link to visit the Microsoft Store page in a browser.
  • On the store page for Halo Infinite, select Get (Free).
  • On the window that pops up, select Get again. This will add the game to your Xbox account.
  • It will automatically begin to download and install. If you have already claimed Halo Infinite game but do not have it installed, install it again by following the steps above. The Get button will be replaced by Install (You own this).

When it is ready to play, you can start the game by hovering over the list of games on the left panel of the Xbox app and selecting Play Halo Infinite.

If you want to remotely install Halo Infinite, go to Remotely install and manage games at Xbox Support for more information.

If you have any issues during installation, please go to Xbox Support for help.

STEAM

To ensure a more stable experience, check Halo Infinite’s minimum and recommended hardware specifications and make sure your PC graphics drivers are up to date.

To install the game, you need to add Halo Infinite to your Steam Library:

  • Search for the “Halo Infinite” page on Steam or use this link to go there directly via browser.

  • Select Play Game. This will add the free game to your Steam Library.

  • Steam will automatically prompt you to install the game. If you need to install the game that is already in your Steam Library in the past:

  • Sign into Steam using the account that has purchased the title.

  • Select Library from the top navigation bar in Steam.

  • Locate Halo Infinite on the left-side navigation bar or in the Your Collections tiles (depending on your default Library view), right-click the game, and select Install. If you have any installation issues, go to Steam Support for help.

How to install on Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S consoles

STORE APP

To install Halo Infinite multiplayer for free on an Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S console.

  • On your Xbox, go to the Store app.
  • Search for “Halo Infinite.” The multiplayer part of the game is free.
  • On the store page for the game, select Get (free).
  • When you add the game to your account, it will automatically start downloading and installing. If you already have Halo Infinite on your Xbox account but it is not downloaded, go to the game’s page in the Store. The Get (free) button will be replaced by an Install (you own this) button.

Once installed, start the game from the Games & Apps menu by highlighting the Halo Infinite tile and press A.

If you want to remotely install Halo Infinite, check Remotely install and manage games at Xbox Support.

If you have any issues during installation, check Xbox Support for help.

GAME PASS APP

  • On your Xbox, go to the Game Pass app.
  • Search for “Halo Infinite.” The multiplayer part of the game is free.
  • On the Game Pass page for the game, select Install.
  • The game will start downloading and installing. Once installed, start the game from the Games & Apps menu by highlighting the Halo Infinite tile and press A.

If you want to remotely install Halo Infinite, check Remotely install and manage games at Xbox Support.

If you have any issues during installation, check Xbox Support for help.

To install Halo Infinite Campaign

If you have purchased Halo Infinite Campaign and it is not available in-game, check that your game is up to date and that you are signed in with the correct Gamertag.

To purchase Campaign, select Campaign in the main menu and follow the prompts to purchase Campaign.

To manage the Campaign installation in-game, follow the steps below:

  • Launch Halo Infinite
  • Open the Control Panel
    • Press Menu on Xbox controller
    • Press ESC or F1 on keyboard
  • Open Manage Game
    • Press Y on a controller
    • Press R on a keyboard
  • Select the Campaign option
    • If the Campaign option in the Manage Game menu is unavailable or cannot be selected, close Halo Infinite and check that your game is up to date.
  • Press Apply
    • The Campaign installation will begin
  • Once the download is complete return to the Main Menu to verify the Campaign installation was successful Halo Infinite is an Xbox Play Anywhere game, this means that if you purchase it on an Xbox console, the Xbox app for PC, or the Microsoft Store app for PC your purchase will carry over to all these storefronts. If you purchase the game through Steam your Campaign purchase will only be available through Steam.

If you experience purchase issues, please contact Xbox or Steam support.

How to Report a Crash to Halo Support

If you’re experiencing crashes in Halo Infinite or Halo: The Master Chief Collection, reporting the issue to Halo Support will help developers investigate and resolve the problem. The more information and reports we receive about a crash, the higher the issue will be on our Halo Support priority stack.

What to include

When reporting a crash, it’s important to provide as much information as possible for developers. Include as much of the following information as possible as well as any additional information you may have:

  • Xbox and PC: Include the step-by-step instructions of what you were doing in-game when the crash occurred. If you have video of the gameplay leading up to the crash, please include that in your report.
  • PC only: Attach a DxDiag file. To create a DxDiag file, type “dxdiag” into the Windows Start menu’s search bar, press the Enter key, then click “Save All Information” when the DirectX Diagnostic Tool pops up.
  • PC only: Include the Problem Report from the Control Panel app. To find this, open the Windows Control Panel and enter “problem reports” in the search bar. Click “View all problem reports” then locate the recent Halo Infinite report. Double click on this Halo Infinite entry then use the “Copy to clipboard” button near the bottom of the window. Finally, paste this text into your ticket’s comments.

How to Report a Crash

Use the Submit a Ticket form to submit your request. Be sure to select the correct game in “Which game is this issue occurring in?” to ensure your crash report is sent to the right development team.

Further Resources

  • If you’re experiencing crashes in multiple games on an Xbox console, Xbox Support may be able to assist you.
  • If Halo Infinite’s performance on PC is below expectations, check whether your PC meets our minimum hardware specifications or the recommended graphics drivers are installed.
    • If your PC meets the hardware specifications and the recommended graphics drivers are installed, try adjusting the in-game video settings to see if your performance improves.

How to Submit a Halo Support Ticket

Bugs are an unintended behavior or malfunction in a program or video game. There are various types of bugs that range in severity. For instance, your character might unexpectedly pass through walls due to graphics glitches, or the game could freeze during certain actions, impacting your overall gameplay experience.

If you encounter a bug in Halo Infinite or any other Halo game, submit a ticket to the Halo Support team. Doing so ensures that the issue is logged in our internal bug database for investigation. The more tickets filed for a specific issue, the higher its priority becomes.

Follow these steps to submit a ticket:

  • Log into your account using the sign in link in the top right corner of the Halo Support site, or click here to sign in.

  • On the home page, scroll down and click on the gray “Submit Report” button as seen in the image below:

  • Fill out the form. Include as much information as possible, such as gameplay clips and screenshots, to help us understand your issue.

    • If you have multiple unrelated issues, submit them as separate tickets.
    • Do not submit multiple tickets for the same issue.
    • Halo Support cannot assist with network, hardware or Microsoft Store purchase issues. You’ll need to go to Xbox Support for that.
    • Try to include details of what you were doing prior to the incident occurring in-game. Some examples include:
      • Were you playing a specific story mission?
      • What area of the game were you in?
      • What type of enemies were you fighting?
      • Were you in a multiplayer match?
      • What mode were you playing?
      • What map were you playing on? Here’s an example of written steps to reproduce a bug (also known as “Repro Steps”) for: “Thruster Pack sound effects not playing”.

  • Launch Halo Infinite

  • Go to the Multiplayer menu

  • Choose any playlist and enter a match

  • While in a match, acquire a Thruster Pack and use it

  • Observe that this equipment does not play its SFX when used If you experience an in-game issue in a Halo game on PC, please include as much of the following information as possible:

  • Attach an up-to-date DxDiagfile. Use the steps below to create a DxDiag file:

    • Type “dxdiag” into the Start menu’s search bar and press the Enter key
    • When the DirectX Diagnostic Tool pops up, click “Save All Information.”
    • Save the file to a location of your preference on your computer.
    • Attach the dxdiag file to the support ticket.

  • If you’re experiencing a crash, include the Problem Report from the Control Panel app. Use the steps below to locate the Problem Report:

    • Open the Control Panel and enter “problem reports” in the search bar.
    • Click “View all problem reports” then locate the recent Halo Infinite report.
    • Double click on this Halo Infinite entry then use the “Copy to clipboard” button near the bottom of the window.
    • Paste the Problem Report text into your ticket’s comments. Be sure to follow the Halo Spartan Code when submitting and managing your ticket.

How to Update Halo Infinite

Many platforms automatically update games. To manually update or verify your game is up-to-date, follow the steps below:

Microsoft Store on PC

  • Close Halo Infinite if it is open
  • Open the Microsoft Store app
    • Type Microsoft Store into the Windows search bar to find it
  • Log in with the Microsoft Account that purchased Halo Infinite
    • To sign out or check what account has automatically signed in, select the profile icon
  • Select Library
  • Scroll down to Halo Infinite
    • Programs with updates available are listed in the Library first
  • Select Update
  • Your update will then download and install If Halo Infinite does not show Update available when it should, select Get updates to refresh the view.

If these instructions do not match your view, you may need to update to the latest version of the Microsoft Store.

If you experience problems updating Halo Infinite, please contact Microsoft Support.

Xbox app on PC

If you try to play Halo and there is an update, you should get a prompt when you try to launch the game. To update without launching the game:

  • Close Halo Infinite if it is open
  • Open Xbox
    • Type Xbox into the Windows search bar to find it
  • Log in with the Gamertag that purchased Halo Infinite
    • To sign out or check what account has automatically signed in, select the profile icon
  • Select the Library icon
  • Select Manage installs
  • Update Halo Infinite
    • In this view players can also turn Automatic updates off or on, pause and resume updates If you experience problems updating Halo Infinite, please contact Xbox Support.

Steam on PC

If you try to play Halo and there is an update, you should get a prompt when you try to launch the game. To update without launching the game:

  • Close Halo Infinite if it is open
  • Open Steam
    • Type Steam into the Windows search bar to find it
  • Log in with the Steam account that purchased Halo Infinite
    • To sign out, select profile name and select Log out of account
  • Select Library
  • Scroll down to Halo Infinite
    • Alternatively, enter Halo Infinite into the search bar
  • Right-click on Halo Infinite
  • Select Update
    • If you do not see the Update option, Halo Infinite is up-to-date. If you experience problems updating Halo Infinite, please contact Steam Support.

Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S Consoles

If you try to play Halo and there is an update, you should get a prompt when you try to launch the game. To update without launching the game:

  • Close Halo Infinite if it is open
  • Select My games & apps
  • Select Manage updates
  • Select Updates
  • Select Halo Infinite and confirm you would like to update
  • Go back to the Manage updates
  • Updating progress will show on this screen. Select Queue for more information, suspend a game if it is running, to pause, resume of cancel updates
    • Suspending or closing an active game can speed up downloads If you experience problems updating Halo Infinite, please contact Xbox Support.

How to turn on automatic updates on Xbox console

Automatic updates can be turned on in System updates:

  • Press the Xbox button
  • Use RB to select Profile and system (user icon)
  • Select Settings
  • Select System
  • Select Updates
  • Select Keep my games & apps up-to-date

Uninstalling

Uninstalling the game removes local game files from your device, but it does not delete your saved progression. Your unlocked missions, discovered collectibles, and other critical progression will remain tied to your account. Some temporary progress, such as mid-mission checkpoints, may be lost.

The following sections cover how to uninstall Halo: Campaign Evolved, based on your platform of choice.

XBOX Series X|S
  • From the home screen, select My games & apps from the top of the screen.
  • In the Games section, find and select Halo: Campaign Evolved.
  • Select Manage (controller with gear icon).
  • Select Uninstall all.
  • Select Uninstall all again to confirm. Halo: Campaign Evolved will then be uninstalled from your console.
PlayStation®5
  • From the home screen, select Settings in the top-right corner.
  • Select Storage.
  • Select Console Storage, or Extended Storage if the files are stored on an external device.
  • Select Games and Apps.
  • Under the Delete Content section, select Halo: Campaign Evolved.
  • Select OK in the pop-up.
  • Select Delete in the bottom right. Halo: Campaign Evolved will then be uninstalled from your console.
Steam
  • Select LIBRARY in the top left.
  • Right-click Halo: Campaign Evolved from the left side bar.
  • Hover over Manage.
  • Select Uninstall.
  • Select the blue Uninstall button to confirm. Halo: Campaign Evolved will then be uninstalled from your computer.
XBOX App PC
  • On your Windows taskbar, select the Windows icon or search bar, if available.
  • Search for XBOX.
  • Select and open the XBOX app.
  • Select My Library on the left side bar.
  • Find and select Halo: Campaign Evolved.
  • Select the three dots icon (…) [More actions button].
  • Select Uninstall.
  • Select Uninstall again to confirm. Halo: Campaign Evolved will then be uninstalled from your computer.
Microsoft Store PC
  • In your Windows taskbar, select the Windows icon or search bar if available, and search for Settings.
  • In Settings, select Apps from the lefthand categories.
  • Select Installed apps.
  • Locate Halo: Campaign Evolved or type Halo: Campaign Evolved in the Search apps search bar.
  • Select the three dots (…) on the righthand side beside the game’s file size.
  • Select Uninstall.
  • Select Uninstall again to confirm. Halo: Campaign Evolved will then be uninstalled from your computer.

Optimizing your PC Experience in Halo: Campaign Evolved

Overview

This PC optimization guide is designed to improve system performance in Halo: Campaign Evolved, with most changes made within the game itself, so your other games are not impacted.

It is recommended to follow the steps in order, as some options may influence your choices for later steps.

Graphics Quality Options

Halo: Campaign Evolved provides 8 individual graphics quality options for balancing your visual fidelity and performance:

  • Effects: Quality and complexity of effects, such as explosions and particles. Lower settings may remove non-essential effects.
  • Geometric: Quality of shapes, such as characters, trees, and rocks.
  • Global Illumination: Quality of light bounce and indirect scene lighting.
  • Lighting: Quality, distance, and amount of shadows.
  • Texture: Resolution of textures.
  • Reflections: Quality of surface reflections.
  • Atmospheric: Quality of elements like the sky, clouds, and fog.
  • Post-processing: Quality of visor effects, lens flares, and other post-effects. Each setting has five options: Very Low, Low, Medium, High, and Ultra. Using lower settings can help boost performance and reduce latency, while using higher settings will increase the fidelity of the visuals at cost of performance and latency.
Very Low

Please note that Very Low settings do not guarantee compatibility or functionality on PC hardware that does not meet the minimum (Low) requirements.

Players experiencing issues on PCs that do not meet the minimum requirements are welcome to submit a ticket, however, please note that Halo Support can only provide limited assistance in these cases.

Handhelds

Players using handheld devices such as the XBOX ROG Ally or Steam Deck are recommended to use Very Low through Medium graphics quality options. Using High or Ultra settings may cause stability issues.

Performance Tip

The Global Illumination Quality and Lighting Quality options control very resource-intensive lighting and shadow systems. Reducing these settings specifically can yield significant increases in performance, without the need to reduce the other graphics options.

To Adjust Your Graphics Settings:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Video.
  • Under the Graphics section, select a value for the Quality Preset setting to adjust all options at once, or manually configure each quality setting.

Upscaling Techniques

Halo: Campaign Evolved includes 4 different upscaling options.

  • NVIDIA Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS)

  • AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR)

  • Intel Xe Super Sampling (XeSS)

    • Available on Steam versions

  • Temporal Super Resolution (TSR) For DLSS, FSR, and XeSS, you can adjust the level of upscaling using the Upscaling Quality dropdown options:

  • Low – 33% resolution

  • Medium – 50% resolution

  • High – 59% resolution

  • Ultra – 67% resolution

  • Native – 100% resolution Higher settings like Native will boost your visual sharpness and clarity at cost of performance, while lower settings like Low will boost your performance at cost of clarity.

To Adjust Upscaling Techniques and Upscaling Quality:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Video.
  • Navigate down to the Advanced section.
  • Adjust Upscaling Technique to your method of choice.
  • Find Upscaling Quality under Upscaling Technique.
Temporal Super Resolution (TSR)

When using TSR, the Upscaling Quality setting does not affect its output resolution. Instead, two dedicated settings are available to adjust how TSR operates:

Resolution Scale

The Resolution Scale setting controls the game’s internal resolution using a percentage of your display resolution. Lowering the value reduces the resolution the game is rendered at, which will reduce system latency and can improve your frames per second (FPS) when not CPU limited. Increasing it above 100% renders the game at a higher-than-native resolution, which can greatly improve image sharpness and clarity, but can come with very high performance cost, depending on how high the percentage is raised.

Minimum Frame Rate

The Minimum Frame Rate setting helps maintain consistent performance by maintaining a target frame rate during demanding moments. To do this, the game automatically adjusts its internal resolution on the fly, lowering it when the FPS drops and raising it again when system demand decreases.

Enabling a minimum frame rate target can improve overall stability and reduce noticeable slowdowns in intensive scenes. Target values that are significantly higher than what your system can deliver may lead to more frequent or drastic changes in image quality as the system works harder to maintain the selected frame rate.

To Adjust Resolution Scale and Minimum Frame Rate Settings:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Video.
  • Under the Frame Rate section, the Minimum Frame Rate option allows you to select a target between 30 FPS and 240 FPS, adjustable in 30 FPS increments.
  • Under the Display section, the Resolution Scale setting allows you to set a value between 50% and 200% of your resolution, adjustable in 10% increments.

Asynchronous Computing

Enabling async compute will allow your GPU to handle multiple workloads at the same time, improving how efficiently it uses its available resources.

In GPU-bound scenarios (where your GPU is the limiting factor), this can increase performance and produce smoother, more consistent frame delivery. In CPU-bound scenarios, leaving it enabled can slightly reduce performance since the GPU is already waiting on the CPU and the extra scheduling work provides little benefit.

As async compute functions differently based on your GPU and accompanying system, it is generally recommended to test the setting yourself:

To Toggle Async Compute On or Off:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Video.
  • Navigate down to the Advanced section.
  • Locate Async Compute and use the toggle to turn it on or off.

Field of View (FOV)

When adjusting FOV, consider balancing visibility and performance. A higher FOV can improve situational awareness and reduce the feeling of tunnel vision, but reduces framerate due to rendering more of the environment on screen at once.

While Field of View is generally set to a specific value for comfort, players with more flexibility may want to reduce their FOV to boost their framerate.

To Adjust Field of View:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Gameplay.
  • Under the Field of View section, you will find two sliders:
    • Field of View: This adjusts your FOV when on foot.
    • 3rd Person Field of View: this adjusts your FOV when in vehicles or using turrets.

Reducing System Load

Minor applications can continue to use system resources even when running in the background. For improved performance, close any unnecessary applications.

Common examples include web browsers, streaming applications, and background launchers.

One of the easiest ways to close applications and refresh your computer is by restarting your system to ensure all background processes are fully cleared before launching the game again.

Turning Off Idle Monitors

Turning off additional active but unused monitors is a lesser-known and completely optional way to improve performance. When multiple displays are active, your system still continuously allocates minor resources to each one, even if they are not being used for gameplay.

Turning off additional monitors can free up system resources, which may improve performance in certain situations, especially on GPU-bound systems.

This step is helpful, but not required. It is intended for players looking to maximize performance.

Frame Generation

Frame Generation adds a generated frame between each fully rendered frame to increase perceived smoothness.

Because these inserted frames are predicted rather than directly tied to player input, this feature increases input latency and may introduce visual errors and artifacting. It is best suited for players who prioritize smoother motion over the most responsive controls.

Frame generation availability depends on your system’s GPU, and choice of upscaling technique:

DLSS
  • NVIDIA: RTX 40-series or newer
FSR
  • NVIDIA: GeForce RTX 20‑series or newer
  • AMD: Radeon RX 5000‑series (RDNA 1) or newer
  • Intel: Intel Arc Alchemist (A‑series) or newer
XeSS

  • NVIDIA: GeForce RTX 20‑series or newer

  • AMD: Radeon RX 5000‑series (RDNA 1) or newer

  • Intel: Intel Arc Alchemist (A‑series) or newer To Toggle Frame Generation On or Off:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).

  • Select Video.

  • Under the Advanced section, you will find the Frame Generation toggle.

    • This setting will be unavailable if your hardware does not support frame generation with your selected upscaling technique.

Frame Rate Limit

This setting limits how many frames your system renders per second. Instead of your hardware running at full capacity to produce as many frames as possible, it only works hard enough to meet the set limit.

Using a frame rate limit can lower GPU and CPU load, decrease power consumption, and reduce heat output. This often results in quieter operation, and more consistent performance with better frame pacing.

To Set a Frame Rate Limit:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Video.
  • Under the Frame Rate section, the Frame Rate Limit option allows you to select a frame rate limit, adjustable in 30 FPS increments.

Low-Latency Mode

Low latency modes reduce the delay between your input and what appears on screen. They do this by limiting how far ahead frames are prepared and displayed, helping ensure your inputs are reflected more quickly. This becomes especially important when using frame generation, where additional buffering can further increase input delay if not managed.

To Enable Low-Latency Modes:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Video.
  • Under the Advanced section, you will find the Low-Latency Mode dropdown.
  • Choose Vendor Specific. The game will automatically choose between NVIDIA Reflex, AMD Anti-Lag, or Intel Xe Low Latency (XeLL), based on what matches your PC hardware.

Vertical Synchronization (VSync)

VSync synchronizes the game’s frame output with your display’s refresh rate to prevent screen tearing, but it can introduce input delay and limit your maximum framerate.

  • Toggle VSync on to reduce or eliminate screen tearing, but expect increased input lag and a capped framerate.

  • Toggle VSync off to allow higher and more responsive framerates, but you may see visible screen tearing. To Toggle VSync On or Off:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).

  • Select Video.

  • Under the Frame Rate section, you will find the VSync toggle. Additional Clarity

VSync limits the game’s frame rate to match your display’s refresh rate. If your display is set to 60 Hz, the frame rate will be capped at 60 FPS. If your display is set to 240 Hz, the frame rate will be capped at 240 FPS. This may also introduce additional delay, as your system may wait until the next display refresh before presenting a completed frame.

Therefore, VSync is best suited for players who are sensitive to screen tearing and are not prioritizing the lowest possible input latency.

Mouse Smoothing

Enabling mouse smoothing averages your mouse input over a short period of time to reduce small, rapid movements. This can make camera motion feel more stable and less jittery, especially at lower frame rates or with inconsistent mouse input.

Turning off mouse smoothing sends your mouse input directly to the game without averaging or filtering. This results in reduced input delay, with a more immediate response to your movements.

To Toggle Mouse Smoothing On or Off:

  • Open the Settings menu using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Keyboard & Mouse.
  • Under the Mouse Sensitivity section, you will find the Mouse Smoothing toggle.
