Halo: The Master Chief Collection Error Message “One or More Actions Are Not Bound to a Key”

If you are seeing this error:

“One or more actions are not bound to a key”

Check that all your actions are bound before playing.

  • Log into the account using the proper Gamertag

  • Navigate to Options & Career

  • Navigate to Settings

  • Select Controls

  • Select Configure Mouse & Keyboard

  • Select Configure Bindings

  • Scroll through the list and make sure each action is bound to a key Alternative method if the above does not work:

  • Log into the account using the proper Gamertag

  • Navigate to Options & Career

  • Navigate to Settings

  • Select Controls

  • Select Configure Mouse & Keyboard

  • Press the Restore Default Settings button

  • Select Restore and back out of the menu to save Note: The alternate method will clear and reset keybindings for every game in Halo: The Master Chief Collection and is only recommended if you cannot figure out the missing keybinding or would like to restore to default settings.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection Known Issues

Updated 7/24/2020

Under Investigation

Hit Registration: We started an initial investigation into this issue in June and are continuing to dive into the code around this. While this is not one of our top issues coming into our support ticket system, it has been a long-standing complaint from many in the community and we will continue to investigate, share our findings with you, and hopefully be able to flight these changes in the future.

Challenges: The team is currently investigating player complaints around challenges and is working on a build update to address the following issues:

  • UI is displaying less progress than players have when rebooting the game.
  • Progress on Challenges is not transferring between Xbox One and PC. Once these issues are resolved internally, we will be preparing a game update to resolve them in the wild.

Halo: Combat Evolved Challenge Progress: We have identified an issue that Halo: Combat Evolved Challenges are not progressing the way they were intended to for Socialite, Breaking a Sweat, Winner is Served, Podium Finish, MP3 Player II, MP3 Player III, and MP3 Player IV. For the time being we have removed the highlight for Halo: Combat Evolved as a possible game to receive progress for these Challenges. We are working to resolve the underlying issues for future Challenges.

Top Community Reported Issues

Co-Op Disconnects: We are aware of reports where players are experiencing disconnects from gameplay while playing cooperatively. We made a couple back end services updates on this issue which have improved it. As well, some folks are reporting that if all players are locked at 60 frames per second, they are seeing this lessen in frequency. We are still attempting to investigate this at this time from player reports. If you are experiencing this problem, please visit the Halo Support site and create a ticket.

Co-Op Latency: At this time, we have not been able to identify any issues around this feature and the functionality is on par with the rest of MCC. There is no active development happening around improving/re-writing the legacy network code around this area of the game. Unfortunately, this would be a massive undertaking and just isn’t within the realm of what the team can currently support.

Achievement Issues: We have continued to fix bugs around reported achievement issues and have been resolving them in each update. If there are achievements that you are still encountering issues with specifically, please submit a ticket at the Halo Support site.

EAC Error Messages in Game: We are continuing work on improving our anti-cheat solution and how we can better support 3rd party applications within that ecosystem. Improvements here will come online as we roll out future patches. As part of our investigation, we’ve enabled more verbose logging. We are continuing to monitor and improve where we can.

Some users have been reporting various EAC error messages appearing while playing. This includes a “UE4 Critical Error,” “You’ve been banned” and others around map files. If you are experiencing any of these, please visit the Halo Support site and create a ticket.

We are currently investigating the UE4 critical errors and believe we have resolved the ban message appearing. If you are receiving the UE4 Critical Error, please make sure you are on the latest version of Windows. Error messages appearing for map files require you to resolve them as the local files have changed around these. In order to resolve these, we recommend you use the “Verify Files” options on Steam and to re-install the game on the Microsoft Store.

Idle Stops Matchmaking Search: This feature is by-design and is done to prevent AKF/idle players from entering matchmaking. This is still on our list but are not actively working on this one as we try to tackle higher priority issues.

Additional Known Issues

  • Prior to installing titles for MCC, users who participated in flights will want to delete all files at C:<UserName>.
  • Players friended only over Steam do not appear in the Roster (must be Xbox Live friends). You can join upon your friends through Steam’s friends list.
  • To send an Xbox Live friend request you will need to use the Game Bar, Xbox Companion app, or add them at Xbox.com
  • When launching in Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, or Korean the voice language pack may not install (Full KBA).
  • If a capture card is set to the default audio input device, all PC audio will transmit over voice channel (Full KBA).
  • Bluetooth headphones will prioritize communication audio after passing the main menu (Full KBA).
  • When moving the game’s window while in Full screen using the Windows, shift, and arrow keys the game may look like a still image.
  • Uninstalling the Steam version of the game with the Microsoft Store version installed will remove the Easy Anti-Cheat client and make the Microsoft Store game be unplayable. To resolve this please uninstall and re-install the Microsoft Store version.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection Legacy User-Generated Content (UGC) Support

To finalize some upgrades to our cloud storage systems, we deprecated our old cloud storage systems in November 2020. As a part of this process we set up a migration plan so that you can quickly and easily migrate any User Generated Content (UGC) created in Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC) on Xbox One if you have only played on PC since December 2019.

When we added PC support for MCC in December 2019 we also updated to a new File Share cloud storage that wasn’t specific to the Xbox. (Which is why we also migrated your Xbox 360 UGC behind the scenes last year!) Previously, your Private and Public File Share items in MCC were stored in this cloud storage.

To migrate your data to the new cloud storage, all you need to do is log in to the Xbox One version of MCC and all of your data will be migrated automatically the first time. When this happens, your Private files will be stored locally on the Xbox One and your Public files will be moved to our new cloud storage.

In short, we updated some systems on the back end to upgrade cloud storage so it would work for PC as well. To finish this update, we’re shutting down our old systems. All you need to do is log in to your Xbox One once, and your files will be migrated safely.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection Patch Notes - 09/22/2020

MCC Update on September 22, 2020

Today, September 22, 2020, we are releasing Halo 3: ODST for the PC. This will include an update for the Xbox version that includes Firefight for ODST. We are also happy to introduce the beginning of Season 3 which will incorporate customization unlocks for titles in the collection along with a journey of continued challenges to complete. A breakdown of the install and update sizes and bug fixes can be found below:

Game Install Size and Version

Please see the information below to ensure you have the proper disk space to install the latest update.

Latest Version

  • The latest version of the game is 1.1829.0.0, to find the version number (Full KBA).

  • To update your game if you are not on the latest version (Full KBA). Microsoft Store and Xbox Game Pass for PC (Beta)

  • Max size of 14.09 GB Steam

  • Max size of 11.5 GB Xbox

  • Max size of 19.74 GB New Features

  • ODST is now available on PC!

  • ODST Firefight has been added to Xbox, Steam, and Windows Store, included with the ODST DLC package.

  • ODST Firefight now supports custom game variant options for creating your own Firefight modes.

  • Season 3 has been added to the collection, featuring ODST Firefight Customization, New Halo 3 Weapon and Visor Skins, and new nameplates including:

    • 12 Halo 3 Weapon Skins.
    • 30 Halo 3 Visor Skins.
    • 10 ODST Character Skins.
    • 4 ODST Character Skins (Unlockable via Challenges).
    • 30 Nameplates.

  • A new frontend menu has been added to welcome ODST Firefight Customization to the collection.

  • Halo 2 Anniversary Multiplayer’s Customization has been broken down into per-part pieces.

  • Added Challenges to the Pause Menu for visibility during gameplay.

  • Added an option that allows users to disable the Challenge notification.

  • Added deck progress counter in Challenge Hub.

  • Progress notifications for featured (golden) challenges now appear gold.

  • More variety is present for Challenges which reward Season Points from week to week.

  • Added ODST’s Silenced SMG, Automag, and Brute Plasma Rifle to Halo 3 Multiplayer.

  • Added Recon weapon set to override all weapons on the map with their ODST counterparts.

  • Added new option for Halo 3 Grenade Regeneration which includes Firebomb grenades.

  • Added bottomless clip option for Halo 3 Infinite Ammo setting.

  • Simplified Chinese Text Language is now supported in ODST. Flight Improvements Brought into MCC Retail

These improvements came from feedback reported by our community and were resolved during or after the flight period of ODST. Thank you for participating!

Halo 3

  • We have brought over the improvements made in our last flight patch to hit registration in multiplayer (related to the 60hz and 30hz engine refresh rate as referenced in our development July 2020 blog).

  • Fixed several issues that caused floating turrets, mongoose falling from the sky, and a series of issues that were identified during the initial flight with Elephants on Sandtrap.

  • Service ID’s shorter than 3 characters now display in gameplay.

  • Scoreboard player scrolling is now bound to Up and Down arrow keys.

  • Updated how the camera intersects with objects in Forge fixing an issue where players would be flung out of the map boundaries and killed when playing or moving objects.

  • Several improvements to Forge with camera movement, menu navigation, and placing or moving objects.

  • Halo 3 matchmaking game films no longer prevent players from restarting the film. ODST

  • Fixed an issue that caused missing or delayed subtitles during cutscenes.

  • Detached turrets no longer use lowered crosshairs when Crosshair Position is set to “Centered”.

  • Players can operate and exit hijacked Ghosts without others seeing them as standing on it.

  • Resolved several crash issues reported during the flight period.

  • All the character models have matching hands.

  • AA Wraith Spawns normally in “Lost Platoon.”

  • Suicide Grunts now have grenades in their hands.

  • Projectiles are visible when Wraiths are seen firing.

  • Players can use health packs in Firefight. Scope zoom sound effects only play once in Firefight.

  • When the time limit expires the game ends instead of a new game starting before the end of the current game in Firefight.

  • Front turrets on Phantoms are visible to players in Firefight

  • The preview images were corrected for several reward tiers (Romeo and Buck, Helmets on/off). Resolved Issues

Below is a breakdown of the specific fixes that have come with today’s update:

General/UI

  • Exit Experience no longer plays sound effects for 0 Challenge XP.

  • Post-game and pause menu roster no longer display player names as “Player Found”.

  • The Refresh Pings button no longer disappears if user passes over Relays option after viewing Network pings.

  • Players will no longer get a duplicate notification of the same challenge when progress is made.

  • The player emblem is no longer missing the background image for all users that appear in the pause menu roster.

  • “Playlist stats” is no longer missing “Max local players” in the “Competitive” game mode selection menu.

  • The warning when enabling a zero-scoring skull has been updated to define that any “mission completion, scoring, time, Challenges, and par achievements will not be recorded when running campaign with a zero-scoring skull. Halo 1

  • The customization menu “Schism” skin texture placement is no longer inconsistent with other Fuel Rod skin textures.

  • The preview model will no longer show the last visor color highlighted when highlighting “DEFAULT” instead of the default color. Halo 2 & Halo 2 Anniversary Multiplayer

  • Armor descriptions are no longer missing from Spartan Armor Customization.

  • In Halo 2 Anniversary Forge, hovering over a different highlightable field before selecting “Yes” on a prompt no longer causes the action to not be taken.

  • Crosshair no longer moves up when zooming if crosshair position is lowered.

  • The Edit Mode action “Grab Object” is no longer assigned to a random key every time the game is restarted. Halo 3

  • Crosshair no longer moves up when zooming if crosshair position is lowered.

  • The prompt no longer indicates [Q] (instead of assigned key) to enter edit mode at the beginning of the forge session.

  • Boot Player prompt no longer contains references to the Xbox One console on PC.

  • Objects placed when nearing the total object limit are now saved.

  • Objects no longer despawn when too many are placed on maps with high object density.

  • Changing to Player Mode while moving an object set to phased physics no longer causes the object to continue moving indefinitely.

  • Forge object rotation is more responsive with a mouse when using an unlimited framerate.

  • Objects set to fixed or phased physics no longer maintain momentum when released and changed to normal physics.

  • Players and held objects are no longer rapidly accelerated when cameras and objects are misaligned.

  • The callout to Summary now reflects actual key binding.

  • The picture-in-picture display in the Sniper Rifle’s Scope will now appropriately reflect the player’s view when the crosshair is centered in Halo 3.

  • The progress bar in Halo 3 Theater is now filled during playback. All weapons, vehicles, and grenades now appear in the appropriate kills category in the Post Game Carnage Report.

  • Halo 3 armor components now display description strings in the Customization menu. ODST

  • Look Inversion set to Inverted no longer overrides Flight Inversion while in Banshee while using Controller.

  • Updated the Epilogue thumbnail & loading screen image to remove a spoiler.

  • Excessive flashing no longer occurs in security camera shots in cutscenes in 4K resolution.

  • Tools of Destruction no longer displays the Halo 3 Magnum instead of ODST Magnum.

  • Suppressed SMG tool of destruction is no longer displayed as standard SMG.

  • There is no longer a large visible gap in the center of the Health Bar in 4K resolution.

  • Com Data UI no longer consistently blinks while viewing any Com Data.

  • Weapon icons in gameplay have been updated to higher-quality versions.

  • Fixed an issue where the VISR’s intel menu did not display objectives as individual bullet points.

  • There is no longer a misplaced period for weapon pickup text in Italian.

  • Betrayed ODSTs no longer appear as Spartans in the Post Game Carnage Report. Halo 4

  • Friendly Fire has been disabled in various Halo 4 Big Team Battle game variants, most notably in Team Heavies. Halo: Reach

  • Engineer is no longer listed as Huragok in the Post Game Carnage Report for ODST and Halo: Reach campaigns.

  • Firefight Matchmaking now gracefully prompts a User without the DLC Entitlement or Campaign Content.

  • Crosshairs no longer move up when zooming if crosshair position is lowered.

  • The picture-in-picture display on Covenant vehicle dashboards will now appropriately reflect the player’s view when the crosshair is centered.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection Patch Notes - 1/29/20

A new game update went live today which includes additional options for Social Matchmaking, additional game content to support events in February, and several bug fixes to areas as it relates to accessibility and stability, as well as improvements to reporting tools behind the scenes.

We know there’s still a sizable list of improvements the community has been vocal about requesting since launch. Many of these issues (PC & Xbox) were known and on the team’s radar prior to launch and some others didn’t surface until the game was out in the wild. With each small patch that doesn’t address these larger lingering issues (i.e. the audio problems some players have experienced) we know it can lead to frustration and disappointment across the community. Please know that the team has been steadily attacking a slew of bugs while also working on quality of life improvements and working towards a larger patch for MCC that will be next up on the release schedule. This will likely entail another flight for Reach as well. We appreciate all the feedback and tickets you’ve filed, and we thank you for your continued support and patience as we work to bring the remaining five titles to MCC on PC.

Here’s the full list of everything included in today’s update:

New Features & Content

Details for the New Features & Content section can be found below in the design update section for rotational playlists, featured content, and events for the month of February.

  • Featured playlists in Match Composer
  • New nameplates for future events
  • New upcoming Matchmaking content Accessibility Bug Fixes

PC Only

  • Fixed an issue where pressing the spacebar would search for a player while typing a Gamertag in the “Find Player” prompt. Global

  • Fixed bugs where pop-up messages were not read properly by Narrator & Xbox Game Transcription.

  • Fixed bugs button prompts were not read properly by Narrator & Xbox Game Transcription.

  • Fixed bugs where on-screen text was not read properly by Narrator & Xbox Game Transcription. General Fixes

Xbox Only

  • Fixed an issue where the Main Menu would not appear after passing the title screen when launching for the first time. Global

  • Fixed a rare crash related to player stats and leaderboards.

  • Reduced some excessive diagnostic reporting to improve performance.

  • Improved player reporting on dedicated servers when identifying potential anti-cheat violations.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection Patch Notes - 12/18/19

Today a small patch is available for MCC on Xbox One and PC which addresses a few specific items the team has been working on. This update has been in development since just prior to launch and is not intended to address many of the issue’s players have been reporting. Most of the current ‘known issues’ and top areas of feedback from players are longer-lead work items that the team is continuing to investigate, and work will continue in the beginning of the new year. To find out more about current known issues go to our MCC known issues page.

Improvements to narration across the front-end interface for Xbox.

One of our top priorities is ensuring that Halo: Reach is accessible to as many players as possible. Today’s patch includes a few updates to further improve accessibility for the title.

Addressed a mechanic for mouse + keyboard players which improves precision of aiming when taking damage.

As part of our ongoing work to assess player feedback across controller and M+KB inputs, the team discovered a legacy mechanic from the original game that was contributing to negative sentiment regarding the feel and responsiveness of playing on M+KB. We have adjusted this mechanic and are interested in what the community thinks of this change. The team will continue to monitor player feedback around controller/M+KB input.

Additional small fixes:

  • Fixed an issue which prevented the sound effect for unlocking a season tier from playing.
  • A stat error has been fixed that was causing multiplayer kills in Halo: Reach to increase the deaths in your service record.
  • A new Halo: Reach themed splash screen has been added to celebrate the inclusion of Reach, our sixth title into Halo: The Master Chief Collection.
  • Resolved an issue that could cause players to be kicked from a matchmade game when an intermittent loss of Xbox Live connectivity occurred.
  • Fixed an exploit where season items which were manually made available while Easy anti-cheat (EAC) was disabled and were able to equip them after launching on an EAC enabled exe.

Playlist Updates

Social 2v2

  • Slayer Removed Solitary and added Synapse (Forge World). Social 4v4

  • Slayer Added Think Twice (Forge World).

  • [Asset Denial] Removed Oddball on Solitary.

  • Made various weighting adjustments. Players will spend a bit less time on Anniversary maps and a bit more time on vanilla maps and classic forge map variants. Social 8v8

  • Slayer Added default variants of Boneyard and Spire. The updated variants (Scrapyard and Spear Broken) will see additional playtesting and refinement before reentering the core map pool.

  • Slayer Added classic Forge World variants Delta Facility and Wayont.

  • Slayer Added new Forge World variants Brick and Hivemind by MythicFritz and Hexduster respectively.

  • Slayer Removed Paradiso (Forge World).

  • [Flag & Bomb] Replaced Neutral Bomb Assault with Multi Bomb Assault on Tempest, Highlands, and Hemorrhage (Forge World). This will reduce the number of matches which end in stalemates.

  • [Flag & Bomb] Added Multi Flag CTF on Brick and Hivemind.

  • [Zone Control] Removed Territories on Breakpoint and High Noon.

  • [Action Sack] Fixed an issue where players could spawn out of bounds on Spear Broken (Spire) and reenabled it for Elite Slayer.

  • Retuned weighting to better balance DLC and vanilla maps. Halo: Reach Hardcore

  • Retuned weighting based on player feedback. Previously, each map / gametype combination held equal weight.

  • Zealot and Sanctuary CTF hold very high weight.

  • Countdown and Pit CTF, Zealot and Sanctuary Slayer, and Nexus KotH hold high weight.

  • Countdown and Battle Canyon Slayer hold medium weight.

  • Battle Canyon KotH holds low weight.

  • Penance Slayer holds very low weight.

New Features

  • Profanity filter: A new option has been added to disable the profanity filter on incoming messages. Disabling the text chat profanity filter will only impact what you see in other players’ messages.
    • Your outgoing messages will still appear filtered from your perspective, even if some other players can read it.
    • By understanding what the filter is hiding, you will know what your teammates with the text filter enabled can see and you can communicate during teamplay more effectively.
  • Season 5 content: Season 5 content has been added to the game files and will become available early next year when Season 5 begins.
  • Tech suits in Halo 3: Tech suits for Halo 3 Spartans are available now in the customization menu.
  • Halo 4 Squad Battle changes:
    • Increased respawn time to 10 seconds in Squad Battle objective games.
    • Reworked Dominion objective ordnance in Squad Battle so that each base has a precision rifle, a grenade, and a power weapon drop. This reduces the total number of power weapons that will be in play at any given time in this game type.
    • Added a jump-up to the Dominion Bravo base from the red side on the “Outcast” map variant used in Squad Battle.

Resolved Issues

Many improvements come from Insiders feedback reported by our community during or after the Flight period of Halo 4. Thank you for participating and please keep submitting tickets! Below is a breakdown of fixes in this update:

Global
  • The default setting for text chat channel availability is now set to All instead of Squad Only.

  • Switching to a second monitor with the resolution scale set to 75% or below should no longer cause menu screens to decrease in size.
  • Switching between fullscreen and borderless modes while using two monitors with certain resolutions will no longer cause the game to switch to the other monitor.
  • Fixed a crash that sometimes occurred if the monitor was set to an unplugged secondary screen.
  • The ping times for the list of selectable servers for matchmaking now refresh properly in the Network tab of the Settings
  • Increasing Brightness settings will no longer change the saturation of objects on Xbox Series X|S.
  • The interface will now display the “Limited Server Region Selected” message when settings are changed from within a matchmaking menu.
  • The push-to-talk button on a gamepad will now update properly when changing the D-Pad & Buttons setting during a game.
  • Players 2, 3, and 4 will now correctly restore their individual settings to default with the Restore default settings
  • On Xbox, signing out of a second active profile will no longer cause the player to lose the ability to change text chat channels.
  • On PC, restoring controls to default settings will now set Preferred Input to Mouse & Keyboard.
  • The UI will no longer display a huge number of unspendable season points if a player somehow ends up with a season points value of -1.
  • Idle users are now kicked during the intermission when the game returns to matchmaking.
Gameplay
  • Fixed an issue causing the “Stick With It… A Little Longer” achievement to unlock early.
  • In the Game Session window, when pressing down to scroll through profiles, the player selection will no longer skip any profiles.
  • Pausing the game while holding down the Push-to-talk voice chat button on a gamepad will no longer cause the user’s mic to stay active indefinitely.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection Patch Notes – 3/3/20

Today, March 3, Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary (H:CEA) joins Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC) on PC and is available for download. To learn more about how you can get in on the action, click HERE. A breakdown of the new features and update size can be found below:

New Features

  • New spartan customization 3D model viewer for H:CEA.
  • A new option in your settings to toggle between either the classic Halo: Combat Evolved (H:CE) multiplayer audio or updated H:CEA audio when playing multiplayer.
  • Halo: Reach has an all new crouch-while-moving behavior added specifically for mouse and keyboard players.
  • The Main Menu’s background video has been updated to celebrate H:CEA joining MCC on PC.
  • Message of the Day (MOTD) has been added on PC to help you stay informed and learn about the latest and greatest things going on in MCC!
  • The option for you to set your controls and key bindings on a per-title basis.
  • Ability to view connection speeds to the datacenters for dedicated used in Online Matchmaking. To view these from in game:
    • Select Options & Career
    • Select Settings
    • Select Network
  • Push-to-talk voice chat and a key binding option have been added. To bind these keys in game:
    • Select Options & Career
    • Select Settings
    • Select Controls
    • Select Configure Mouse & Keyboard
    • Set the desired keys
  • Updated zoom controls have been implemented for all titles.
  • Additional Competitive and Social matchmaking options for H:CEA.

Game Install Size and Version

Please see the information below to ensure you have proper disk space to install each title from your desired store platform as well as are on the latest update.

Latest Version

  • MCC Bundle Owners: A 12.1 GB update with both Halo: Reach and H:CEA being about 43 GB installed.

  • H:CEA Owners: A 15.7 GB download for a total of about 17 GB installed.

  • Halo: Reach Owners: A 20.4 GB download for a total of about 31 GB installed.

Resolved Community Issues

Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary

Significant improvements have been made. These include:

  • Improved game stability resolving several crashes.
  • Player became invisible in a Ghost by boarding the vehicle while entering a teleporter.
  • HUD positioning better reflects legacy.
  • Respawn beep sound effects have a lower pitch than in legacy Halo: CE.
  • Multiple remastered sound effects playing in H:CE multiplayer when set to “Classic.”
  • Added ability to set primary and secondary weapon in custom games.
  • Sometimes controller vibration continues when pausing the title.
  • Player name appearing during camouflaged states better reflects legacy.
  • Plasma projectiles from Type-25 Spirit are now aligned with the turrets.
Halo: Reach

Can’t Crouch While Moving: The way crouching and moving worked in Halo: Reach when it shipped was currently true to the way it worked in the original game on Xbox 360. This has changed. Players now have the option to crouch while move when using Keyboard and Mouse

  • Animations and help bar are missing when exiting a multiplayer match in Halo: Reach.
  • Occasionally, inputs from a controller on the Pause Menu will not be reflected in Halo: Reach multiplayer and campaign.
  • Audio is silent or too quiet during intro cinematics when playing from mission to mission.

How to Change Field-Of-View (FOV) Options in Halo: The Master Chief Collection

Increasing the Field-of-View (FOV) setting can allow you to see more of the battlefield at once and can reduce the feeling of “tunnel vision” that some players may experience.

To change the FOV setting in Halo: The Master Chief Collection:

  • From the main menu, choose Options & Career.

  • Choose Settings.

  • By default, you’ll arrive on the Controls tab of the Settings menu. Switch to the Video tab.

  • Scroll down to the Video Settings section.

  • Adjust the Field-of-View slider to your preference. A higher number will widen the Field-of-View to show more of the environment on screen at once.

  • It is recommended that you choose Set for all games at the bottom of the screen.

  • Choose Yes when asked if you are sure. However, if you’d like to set FOV on a per-game basis, use these additional steps:

  • Right above the Video Settings section is a small section called Game Setting. Change this to match the specific Halo game you want to change the FOV for.

  • When you are done adjusting FOV, choose Back in the bottom left of the screen.

  • Choose Save Settings when prompted. The process for changing the FOV setting is the same on both console and PC.

How to Change Your Display Settings in Halo: The Master Chief Collection on PC

Making sure your game’s display and video settings are set up properly can reduce issues like screen tearing or stuttering.

First, you will need to know your screen’s resolution. If the steps below do not help, you can refer to this article for additional information.

  • Press the Windows key

  • Select Setting

  • Select System

  • Select Display

  • Scroll down and locate the Resolution box and take note of your screen’s resolution To change your game’s display settings to match your screen’s:

  • Launch Halo: The Master Chief Collection on PC

  • Navigate to Options and Career from the bottom of the screen

  • Select Settings

  • Select Video

  • Set this resolution to match the screen resolution you confirmed earlier Restart your game after changing and saving your settings for best performance.

How to Claim Halo Twitch Drops

Players can earn in-game content for both Halo Infinite and Halo: The Master Chief Collection by participating in Halo events on Twitch.tv. These rewards are called Twitch Drops and are only available for a limited time. The rewards and their unlock requirements can vary between events, so make sure to check the details of any event.

To earn Twitch Drops, you need to have a Twitch account and be signed into Twitch while you are earning the reward. See Create an Account with Twitch for more information.

Once you have earned a Twitch Drop it will be visible in your Twitch Drops Inventory. You need to link your Twitch account through Halo Waypoint before you can claim your rewards.

Important Notes on Twitch Drop Troubleshooting

  • For help with your Twitch account, please contact Twitch support.
    • The Twitch support website will also have the most up-to-date information about ongoing outages affecting Drops and other parts of the site, which may explain your issue.
  • Halo Support cannot grant Twitch Drop rewards or assist with linking accounts. Please note that only one Halo Waypoint account may be linked to your Twitch account at any given time.
    • To ensure fulfilment of your Twitch Drop rewards, link your Waypoint account to your Twitch account within 14 days of the end of the Drop campaign.
  • If you recently changed your password on Twitch.tv, your Twitch account may have been unlinked from Halo Waypoint. Follow the instructions included in Step 1 below to relink your accounts.
  • Progress towards receiving a Drop may be affected by the following factors:
    • You must be logged into the account linked to your Waypoint account and watch an affiliated livestream to make progress towards a Twitch Drop. Videos on Demand (VODs) do not count towards this progress.
    • Progress is only counted when you watch an affiliated stream via the website on PC/Mac or, if using an Android or iOS device, the official Twitch app.
    • Having multiple Twitch pages open at once may interrupt Twitch Drop progression, as outlined on the Twitch support website:
      • If there are multiple channels affiliated with the same Drop, your progress will not accrue more quickly if you watch all of them simultaneously. However, your progress will carry over should you choose to watch a different channel affiliated with the same Drop campaign.
      • Watching multiple channels for different Drops campaigns will also hinder your progress.
      • If your active Twitch Drop appears to have stopped progressing, close any other browser windows or tabs that have Twitch open, then refresh the page with the active Twitch Drop.
    • Browser extensions may sometimes interfere with Drop progress. Try disabling your browser extensions if your progress is not tracking.
  • If you have not received your Drop in-game, check that you’ve completed the Drop’s requirements on Twitch and that your Twitch account is properly connected to your Halo Waypoint account. Submit a ticket using the link at the bottom of this article if your account still has not received the Drop reward(s) within 24 hours. Halo Support can flag the issue to our developers for further investigation and to help us improve future Twitch Drops.
  • Visit the Twitch support website for more information on how Twitch Drops work.

How to claim Halo Twitch Drop rewards

Step 1: Link your Twitch account to your Halo Waypoint profile:
- Go to [halowaypoint.com](https://www.halowaypoint.com/) and sign in with your Xbox Live account.
    - Make sure you have signed into the correct Gamertag.
    - You can also access the Halo Waypoint site by selecting Connect on a Halo reward in your Twitch Drops Inventory.
- Click on your profile picture and select Settings.
- Go to Linked Accounts and select Link Twitch.
- If you are not already signed into Twitch, a popup will appear. Sign into your Twitch account.
- Confirm you wish to authorize 343 Industries to connect to your Twitch account.
- Initially you may see your account is listed as …, but if you refresh your browser window your account should display Status: Account Connected. If that does not work you may need to unlink and relink your account.
Step 2: Claim items from your Twitch Drops Inventory
- See [How to Discover and Claim Drops on Twitch](https://help.twitch.tv/s/article/mission-based-drops?language=en_US) for more information.
- Drops can only be claimed once per account.
- Halo: The Master Chief Collection Twitch Drops: after claiming the reward in your Twitch Drops Inventory, sign into Halo Waypoint and navigate to the [Twitch Drops Redemption](https://www.halowaypoint.com/redeem?view=twitch-drops) page. The recently claimed Twitch Drop should be listed at or near the top of this page. Select the Claim button listed alongside the recently earned reward to complete the Twitch Drop redemption.
Step 3: Cosmetic items can then be accessed from the Customize menu
- Some cosmetics only apply to a specific armor core or weapon type.
- It may take some time for an item to appear. If it does not appear, check that you are signed in with the correct Gamertag, and try restarting your game.

Twitch Drop troubleshooting

If you have completed the requirements for a Twitch Drop but the rewards are not available in-game, follow the steps below to verify your accounts are linked and to manually grant unclaimed rewards.

  • Navigate to HaloWaypoint.com and, using the Sign In button in the top right corner, sign into your Xbox account.

  • After signing in, click on your profile’s avatar in the top right corner of the page and select Drops & Code Redemption.

  • On the Drops & Code Redemption page, select the Twitch Drops tab.

    • If your Halo Waypoint and Twitch accounts are not linked, use the Link Twitch button on this page to connect your accounts.

  • The Twitch Drops tab shows the status of all Twitch Drops earned on your linked Twitch account. If a Drop’s status is displayed as “Claimed” then it will be available for use in the associated Halo title (either Halo Infinite or Halo: The Master Chief Collection). If there is a “Claim” button in the Status column, the Drop has been earned on Twitch but it was not granted by Halo Waypoint. Click on the “Claim” button to manually grant this item to your account.

    • If a Twitch Drop reward is not listed on this page, navigate to your Twitch Drops inventory to confirm that you have completed the requirements and that the reward is ready to be claimed.

  • After manually granting the item with the “Claim” button, launch either Halo Infinite or Halo: The Master Chief Collection and navigate to the Customize menu to equip your reward. How to change the Twitch account associated with Halo Waypoint

  • Go to Twitch.tv Connection settings and sign in with the account associated with Halo Waypoint.

  • Scroll down to Other Connections and find 343 Industries.

  • Select Disconnect and confirm you wish to disconnect.

  • Sign out of Twitch and then sign in with the account you prefer.

  • Go to halowaypoint.com and sign in with your Xbox Live account.

  • Click on your profile picture and select Settings.

  • Go to Linked Accounts and select Unlink Twitch if it is still displaying the old account.

  • Select Link Twitch and follow the prompts to connect the accounts. Unlinking and linking your account may help future Twitch rewards appear

If your rewards still do not appear in your Redemption History, you may need to unlink and re-link your account to get future Twitch Drops. Rewards will not be retroactively granted, but this will refresh the connection. You can unlink and link your account by following the steps for changing your Twitch account, but skip signing out of your Twitch account.

If rewards appear in your Redemption History but have not appeared in-game

  • Wait 24 hours, sometimes rewards are delayed.
  • Restart either Halo Infinite or Halo: The Master Chief Collection.
  • If your rewards still have not arrived, please send us a support ticket.
    • Halo Support cannot provide missing rewards, but your data will give our developers valuable information.
    • Please include the following screenshots in your Halo Support ticket:
      • A screenshot of your Twitch Drops inventory showing the Twitch Drop as completed.
      • A screenshot of your Halo Waypoint Twitch Drops history.
      • A screenshot of your Halo Waypoint redemption history.
      • A screenshot of your linked Twitch account on Halo Waypoint.

Encountering issues with a claimed Twitch Drop?

Sign in to submit a Twitch Drop bug report.

How to Download and Play Mods for Halo: The Master Chief Collection via the Steam Workshop

Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC) supports the Steam Workshop, which enables players to find, download, and play mods created by other Halo players. Installing mods via the Steam Workshop allows for all new experiences in the Master Chief Collection, such as:

  • Multiplayer and Firefight maps
  • Weapons, equipment, and other gameplay tweaks
  • Custom campaigns. Halo Support is unable to provide troubleshooting or guidance with mods and mod development. If you want to discuss modding with other players, please go to the Halo: The Master Chief Collection’s Modding sub-forum on Steam and join the community there.

Finding, Downloading, and Playing Mods

To get started:

  • Launch Steam and open the Library tab.
  • In the left column locate Halo: The Master Chief Collection and click it once to open the Steam page for MCC.
  • Open the tab titled Workshop (or click this link).
  • On the Workshop page you can browse through a wide variety of mods.
    • Each mod page provides a description, screenshots, reviews and comments from other players.
    • It’s important to review the mod’s description for specific information about the mod. Make note of what game the mod is for, and whether it is for Campaign, Multiplayer, or Firefight. The mod’s description usually has information from the mod creator regarding compatible game modes and other setup instructions. Read through the mod’s description to ensure you understand how the mod works.
  • To install the mod, click on the green Subscribe button.
    • This will download the mod to your system. You can track the progress of the install at the bottom of the Steam client window, or by mousing over the Library tab and selecting Downloads.
  • Once you’ve downloaded a mod, launch Halo: The Master Chief Collection by clicking the Library tab and double clicking Halo: The Master Chief Collection.
  • Select “Play Halo MCC Anti-Cheat Disabled” and click the blue Play button.
    • Note: mods will not work unless Easy Anti-Cheat is disabled.
  • Follow the mod instructions from the Steam Workshop page on how to find and launch the mod. When playing on a modded map you can normally customize the settings the same as an official map in the Missions menu before launching. Check the mod’s description to confirm.

Removing Mods

When you want to remove a mod:

  • Launch Steam and open the Library tab.
  • In the left column locate Halo: The Master Chief Collection and click it once to open the Steam Page for MCC.
  • Open the tab titled Workshop (or click this link).
  • Mouse over the Browse button and select Subscribed Items.
  • Locate the mod you want to remove and click the Subscribed button to automatically remove the mod.

Additional Mod Support

Halo Support is unable to provide troubleshooting or guidance with mods and mod development. If you want to discuss modding with other players, please go to the Halo: The Master Chief Collection’s Modding sub-forum on Steam and join the community there.

How to Find Your Version Number for Halo: The Master Chief Collection

To identify the version number for your game, please choose your platform below.

Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S

  • Turn on your console and sign in using the account that owns the game
  • Navigate to your game by:
    • Pressing the jewel button and scrolling down to “My games and apps”
    • Selecting “See all”
  • Highlight the game tile
  • Press the Start button (3 horizontal lines)
  • Scroll down and select Manage game & add-ons
  • Observe the Version number in the top right of your screen

Steam (PC)

  • Open Steam by pressing the Windows key and typing “Steam”
  • Launch Steam
  • Select Library from the window that opens
  • Scroll down to Halo: The Master Chief Collection on the left side
  • Right click on the title
  • Select Properties
  • Select Local Files from the ribbon at the top of the menu
  • Select Browse Local Files
  • Navigate to the folder titled MCC and double-click
  • Locate the folder called Binaries and double-click
  • Double-click on the Win6 folder
    • Full, final file path should be C:Files (x86)The Master Chief Collection
  • Locate the file titled MCC-Win64-Shipping.exe
  • Right click the file and select Properties
  • From the Properties menu, select the Details tab in the top ribbon
  • Locate the File version and ensure it matches the latest version (see latest patch notes for additional info)

Microsoft Store (PC)

  • Press the Windows key and search for “Apps & features” and open the menu
  • Search for Halo: The Master Chief Collection in the search box (or scroll through the list)
  • Once located, click on Halo: The Master Chief Collection
  • Select Advanced options
  • Locate Specifications and look at version and ensure it matches the latest version (see latest patch notes for additional info)

How to Fix the Xbox Network Sign-Out Loop with Halo: The Master Chief Collection on Steam

To sign out of your Xbox network Account on Steam:

  • From the main menu, press R to open your Active Roster
  • Click on your Gamertag
  • Select Change Profile
  • Select Yes on the confirmation screen to log out of the Xbox network.

Resolving the endless sign-out loop

When signing in with an account that has never played Halo: The Master Chief Collection before, you will be presented with a “Let this app access your info” prompt. If you declined this prompt, you will not be able to play. Some users are reporting they are unable to sign out at this point after selecting no. When trying to sign in again, the sign in window will attempt to appear, but result in an error and not allow a user to sign in.

If you are stuck in this loop, you will need to to remove the webcache data contained in your Windows users AppData folder. Below are the steps to locate and remove the files to exit this loop:

  • Navigate to your local AppData’s webcache folder at C:
    • Alternatively, paste this into your explorer window bar: %userprofile%
  • Delete all files in this location
  • Launch the game
  • Sign into the preferred Xbox network account and allow the app to access your info

How to Install Halo: The Master Chief Collection on Xbox Consoles, Steam, Microsoft Store, and PC Game Pass

The steps to install Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC) are different depending on which platform you’re playing on. Make sure you check the correct section below.

Xbox Game Pass (on PC)

If you have an active subscription to a PC Game Pass that includes Halo: The Master Chief Collection, you can play Halo: The Master Chief Collection including Halo: Reach and Halo 3: ODST on your PC through the Xbox PC app. You can check the Halo: The Master Chief Collection on the Xbox Store to see which Game Passes it’s available on.

Here’s how:

  • Download the Xbox app for PC and launch it.
  • Sign in using your account with an active Xbox Game Pass subscription.
  • Type “Halo” in the search bar in the top right of the app and search.
  • Select Halo: The Master Chief Collection from the search results.
  • Click the Install button.

Xbox Game Pass (on Console)

If you subscribed to a Game Pass that includes Halo: The Master Chief Collection, you can play Halo: The Master Chief Collection as part of your subscription. This includes the Halo: Reach DLC. You can check the Halo: The Master Chief Collection on the Xbox Store to see which Game Passes it’s available on.

To play:

  • Sign in to your Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S console using your account with the applicable Xbox Game Pass subscription.
  • Press the Guide button (the Xbox logo button in the center of the controller) and navigate to the “Store.”
  • In the store, press Left Bumper (LB) to navigate to the “Game Pass” menu bar
  • Navigate to Halo: The Master Chief Collection and press A.
  • Select Install from the bar that pops up.

Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S Console

This section applies to people who own Halo: The Master Chief Collection without Xbox Game pass.

If you already own Halo: The Master Chief Collection on Xbox One, Halo: Reach and Halo 3: ODST will be listed as separate DLC items for purchase in the Microsoft Store.

On your Xbox One console:

  • Navigate to the Halo: The Master Chief Collection tile in your Games & Apps and press the menu button.
  • Scroll down to Manage game & add-ons and press A
  • On the left-hand side, scroll down to Ready to install and press A
  • Select your choices on the right and install them.

Steam

When you purchase the game, the store will automatically prompt you to install it.

If you need to install the game any other time:

  • Sign in to Steam using the account that purchased the title
  • Select Library from the top navigation bar in Steam.
  • Locate the game on the left-side navigation bar, right-click it, and select Install.

Microsoft Store (PC)

When you purchase the game, the store will automatically prompt you to install it.

If you need to install the game any other time:

  • Check to make sure you are signed in to your PC using the correct account.
  • On your keyboard, press the Windows key and type “Store” in the search bar to bring up the Microsoft Store app.
    • You can navigate to or open the Microsoft Store however you like; this is just one way to do it.
  • In the Windows Store app, navigate to the top right and click the […] next to your account’s profile picture
  • Select “Downloads and updates”
  • On the left-hand side, select “Ready to install”
  • Find the game in the list and select “Install”

How to Launch Halo: The Master Chief Collection with Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) Disabled

To launch Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC) with Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) disabled on the Xbox app for PC or on Steam:

Steam

Navigate to Halo: The Master Chief Collection in the Steam client’s Library tab, then press the Play button on its page. In the window that pops up, select “Play Halo: MCC Anti-Cheat Disabled (Mods and Limited Services)” and click the Play button.

Screenshot of the Launch Option pop-up window in Steam.

To launch MCC with EAC enabled again, fully exit the game then choose the other option shown above (“Play Halo: The Master Chief Collection”) when you launch Halo: MCC on Steam.

Microsoft Store and Xbox apps

In the Windows search field search for MCC. From the results, select “Halo: MCC Anti-Cheat Disabled (Mods and Limited Services)” to launch Halo: MCC with EAC disabled.

Screenshot of the game as it appears in Windows search menu.

To launch MCC with EAC enabled again, fully exit the game and launch normally from the Microsoft Store app.

Changes when playing with Easy Anti-Cheat Disabled

There are several important things to consider when playing MCC with EAC disabled:

  • While playing with Easy Anti-Chat Disabled the public matchmaking features will be unavailable.
    • If you click on matchmaking menu items while EAC is disabled, you’ll get an alert that says “Anti-Cheat Incident – You cannot access this feature because Easy Anti-Cheat isn’t enabled.”
  • You can modify game files and content, then play online through Custom Games and campaign missions.
  • If you’re having issues playing MCC with EAC enabled after installing mods, you may need to restore the game files to their original state.
    • If you are not familiar with modding and altering core files, be careful - you could accidentally leave your game files in an unplayable state, requiring a full re-installation. It’s recommended to make a backup of core game files before attempting any modding.

Steps for repairing or verifying game installation

Steam
  • Open your Steam client and navigate the Library tab.
  • In the Library list of games (left column of the Steam client), right-click on Halo: The Master Chief Collection and select Properties.
  • Click on Installed Files and click the “Verify integrity of game files” button.
  • Wait for the verification process to complete. This can take a few minutes.
  • Once complete the green PLAY button will be available. Screenshot of the Properties menu on Steam.
Xbox and Microsoft Store app
  • Open the Xbox app on your Windows PC.
  • In the left menu of the Xbox app located the Most Recent or Installed Menu and open Halo: The Master Chief Collection.
  • Click the ellipse button (3 dots) located near the top of the page. Select Manage from the drop-down menu.
  • Click the Files tab.
  • Click Verify and Repair.
  • Read the warning pop-up and click Yes.
  • A green status button will show near the top of the screen.
  • When the repair is complete the status button will change to a green PLAY button. Screenshot of the Manage menu on the Xbox app.

I Can’t Access My Downloadable Content (DLC) on the Microsoft Store

If you own Halo: The Master Chief Collection through the Microsoft Store and are experiencing issues seeing purchased DLC in-game, follow these steps:

  • If your game is open, close it.
  • Launch the Microsoft Store and check the account signed in using the profile in the top-right
    • The account signed in should be the same account that purchased the game and DLC
  • Launch the Xbox App.
  • Check that the account signed into the app matches that signed into the Microsoft Store.
    • If the Gamertags match, launch your game and the DLC should appear
    • If the Gamertags do not match, please make sure you are signed into both the Xbox app and the Microsoft Store using the same Gamertag then launch MCC. Note:

Using a VPN can cause the same issue. We recommend disabling your VPN, launching the title, and checking whether the problem persists. If the problem has been resolved, you should then be able to re-enable your VPN and play.

I Can’t Download Language Packs from the Microsoft Store

Players using the Microsoft Store version of Halo: The Master Chief Collection for PC may have issues downloading some or all language packs.

Restarting your PC should solve this problem. Note, this is restarting your entire system, not just the game.

For issues with the functionality or accuracy of installed language packs in-game, submit an MCC bug report.

  • Select the Bluetooth profile identifying your device as headphones, not a headset or speaker. In the example below, we would select the second option in the list, “Headphones (Bose Headphones Stereo).”

My Achievement or Challenge Didn’t Unlock. Can Halo Support Give Me Credit for It?

Halo Support gladly accept tickets about issues with achievements and challenges to report them to the developers, but we can’t guarantee a fix or give credit for completion.

Unfortunately, there is no way to retroactively issue achievement credit or challenge rewards to players.

To troubleshoot possible reasons why achievements won’t unlock, check Achievement progression and unlock issues (This article doesn’t apply to issues with challenge progress).

Quick Start Guide for Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC)

This guide quickly introduces the various ways to play in Halo: The Master Chief Collection and explains how to team up with friends. If you’re new, this is a good place to start. If you need help getting the game installed, check How to Install Halo: the Master Chief Collection.

  • What is in Halo: The Master Chief Collection?
  • How to play Halo: The Master Chief Collection
  • Where to start as a new player in Halo: The Master Chief Collection
  • How to play Halo: The Master Chief Collection with friends
  • How to use splitscreen to play Halo: the Master Chief Collection multiplayer on an Xbox console
  • How to play Halo: the Master Chief Collection online with friends using the Xbox network
    • How to add your Xbox network friend to your Roster in Halo: the Master Chief Collection
      • On an Xbox console
      • On PC

What is in Halo: The Master Chief Collection?

Halo: The Master Chief Collection is the ultimate way to play six different Halo games spanning over ten years. It’s available on both Xbox and Windows platforms, for direct purchase or through some Xbox Game Passes.

Halo: The Master Chief Collection includes (in order of original release date):

  • Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary
  • Halo 2 Anniversary
  • Halo 3
  • Halo 3: ODST
  • Halo: Reach
  • Halo 4 Each game in the series plays a little bit differently.

How to play Halo: The Master Chief Collection

There are many ways to play Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC), and all of them can be accessed from the main menu once you start the game on your Xbox or PC.

There are 3 main ways to play:

  • Campaigns are individual challenges that take you through the game’s story in a logical order.
    • You can play with friends on the same Xbox console via splitscreen.
    • On PC, you can play with friends over the Xbox network, but you can’t use splitscreen.
  • Multiplayer is where you can join other players in a match against real people online. If your friends are online or you’re playing with them in splitscreen, you can play with them too.
  • Firefight is where you can defend against waves of computer-controlled enemy force. You can play alone or with other players.

Where to start as a new player in Halo: The Master Chief Collection

To start playing Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC), you’ll want to choose Campaigns, Multiplayer, or Firefight from the main menu. The main menu is the one that appears after you press Start or Enter on the initial screen with the MCC logo.

If you’re totally new to Halo games, we recommend starting with a Campaign. To experience the games in the order they released, start with the Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary campaign.

To start playing a Campaign:

  • On the main menu, select Campaigns.
  • A list of each game within MCC will appear. We recommend starting with Halo: CE Anniversary, but you can select whichever.
  • Next, if you’re new to Halo, we recommend you select Quick Start so you can quickly get to playing the campaign.
  • On the Difficulty selection menu, choose a difficulty according to your skill level. Easy or Normal are the best choices for a new player. After choosing a difficulty, the campaign mode will start.

In the future, to continue playing where you left off, select Resume instead of Quick Start at step 3.

How to play Halo: The Master Chief Collection with friends

You can play almost every part of Halo: The Master Chief Collection online using the Xbox network or with friends right next you with splitscreen.

Splitscreen is the term for when 2 or more people are playing on the same Xbox and the same screen. The screen is “split” to give each person their own section to play.

You can also play online with friends as long as they have their own copy of Halo: The Master Chief Collection and an Xbox account.

How to use splitscreen to play Halo: the Master Chief Collection multiplayer on an Xbox console

You will need two Xbox controllers connected to the Xbox console to use splitscreen.

  • After starting Halo: The Master Chief Collection and getting to the main menu, press the X button on your Xbox controller to bring up the Roster The Roster menu is how you add people to your group and play Halo with them.
  • You should see your name at the top of the list under a My Game Session banner on the right side of the screen.
  • Have your friend press the A button on the second Xbox controller.
  • A side panel will appear so your friend can select an Xbox profile to use.
    • If your friend doesn’t already have a profile, they can create one of their own, or select Add guest near the bottom of the panel so they can quickly jump in with a temporary profile.
    • A temporary profile will not keep any save data once it signs out.
  • Once your friend has signed into a profile, you will be returned to the Roster. Your friend’s profile will be shown underneath yours. Now, when you start a Campaign, play in Firefight, or play in a Multiplayer playlist, your friend will be with you and will be on your team (if applicable).

You can have up to 4 people play at the same time on the same Xbox console by using splitscreen. As long as you have an Xbox controller for each player, just add the 3rd and 4th person to the game the same way.

However, when playing with more than two people in splitscreen, only Multiplayer is available.

How to play Halo: the Master Chief Collection online with friends using the Xbox network

You can play online with a friend who has their own Halo: The Master Chief Collection game. If you want, you can even play with a friend who is playing on a PC while you are playing on an Xbox console using cross-play (don’t worry, that happens automatically). Campaign and Campaign Playlists currently cannot use cross-play.

To play with friends online, you must first add them as a friend on your Xbox account. Visit How to add new Xbox friends | Xbox Support for detailed steps for adding friends.

To invite your Xbox network friend to your Roster in Halo: the Master Chief Collection:

Once the person you would like to play with has been added as your friend on the Xbox network, it’s time to invite them to your Roster within Halo: The Master Chief Collection. This will make sure they join your game sessions with you. You’ll need to invite any friends you’d like to play with to your Roster each time you close and restart Halo: The Master Chief Collection.

To add your friend to your Roster:

On an Xbox console:
  • Once both you and your friend are at the main menu of Halo: The Master Chief Collection, press the X button.
  • In the Roster panel that appears on the right side of the screen, you should see your friend.
  • Highlight your friend’s name and press the A button to select them.
  • Select Invite Player with the A button to send them a game invite.
  • When your friend receives and accepts the game invite, their name will appear in the Roster list underneath My game session. You are now ready to play together!
On PC:
  • Once you and your friends are both at the main menu of Halo: The Master Chief Collection, click the Roster button in the top-right of the screen.
  • In the Roster panel that appears on the right side of the screen, you should see your friend.
  • Click your friend’s name and select Invite Player.
  • When your friend receives and accepts the game invite, their name will appear in the Roster list underneath My game session. You are now ready to play together!

Requirements to Play Halo: The Master Chief Collection Online

You need an Xbox network account to play online on any platform that offers Halo: The Master Chief Collection, but you might need an additional type of account depending on what platform you use. Check your platform below.

Note: Creating new accounts if you have been banned violates Xbox Community Standards and is not permitted.

Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S Console

To play Halo: The Master Chief Collection online on an Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S console:

  • You need an Xbox network account. If you don’t have one, you can create one for free.
  • You need an active Game Pass Subscription. If you forgot your Xbox network account login information, Xbox Support can help.

Microsoft Store (PC)

To play Halo: The Master Chief Collection online on a PC through the Microsoft Store:

  • You need an Xbox network account. If you don’t have one, you can create one for free.
  • If you bought the game on the Microsoft Store, you do not need an active Game Pass subscription to play.
  • If you’re using Game Pass for PC to access the game, you will need an active subscription for a Game Pass that includes Halo: The Master Chief Collection. You can check the Halo: The Master Chief Collection on the Xbox Store to see which Game Passes it’s available on. If you forgot your Xbox network account login information, Xbox Support can help.

Steam Games (PC)

To play Halo: The Master Chief Collection online on a PC through Steam:

  • You need an Xbox network account. If you don’t have one, you can create one for free.
  • You do not need an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to play. If you forgot your Xbox network account login information, Xbox Support can help.

Saved Data and Settings May Be Lost When Updating Halo: The Master Chief Collection

Some improvements to the game require us to make changes that will invalidate past saved data (mainly impacting films and campaign saves). This includes your mid-mission progress (in and out of playlists), any Theater films, and game options such as input bindings and video settings. The saved content missing may be different depending on the platform. This does not impact achievements.

As Halo: The Master Chief Collection only supports temporary Theater films, we strongly suggest that you record your favorite moments soon after generating the film, using GameDVR or your preferred recording method. Do this early to avoid loss of data during a title update.

Updating Halo: The Master Chief Collection on PC

Steam should auto-update your game. If your game does not update automatically:

  • On your keyboard, press the Windows key and type “Steam” in the search bar to locate and open the Steam app.

  • Select Library in the top navigation bar.

  • Look through the list of games on the left side of the screen (or use search) for Halo: The Master Chief Collection, then right-click the title.

  • Select Update. If you are using the Microsoft Store version on PC:

  • On your keyboard, press the Windows key and type in “Microsoft Store” to locate and open the Microsoft Store app.

  • Log into the Microsoft Store app using the same Microsoft Account you used to purchase your game.

  • In the top-right corner of the Microsoft Store app, click on “…” to the right of your profile avatar.

  • Select Get Updates. The updates for the Xbox Insider Hub app will appear on this screen.

  • On the same “Downloads and Updates” screen, select the Update All button if they do not start downloading automatically.

What Is the Difference between “Co-op,” Firefight, and Spartan Ops in Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC)?

In Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC), most story-based modes can be played either single-player or with friends. Playing any of these single-player modes with friends can be referred to as playing cooperatively, or “co-op.” However, it is most common for players to refer to playing Campaign missions with a friend as “playing co-op.”

The difference between co-op Campaign, Firefight, and Spartan Ops can be confusing for newer players. Here is an explanation of the differences:

Co-op Campaign

Co-op broadly refers to having more than one player in the game cooperating (you can’t “cooperate” without a friend around to cooperate with). You can play co-op in any of the Campaigns, Firefight, and Spartan Ops.

When someone says “playing co-op” without specifying any mode in a Halo game, they are usually referring to playing Campaign missions with a friend.

  • Halo: Combat Evolved and Halo 2 support co-op Campaign up to two players.
  • Halo 3, Halo 3: ODST, Halo: Reach, and Halo 4 support co-op Campaigns up to four players, but only two players can split a screen at a time (splitscreen is Xbox only).

Firefight

Firefight is a game mode in Halo 3: ODST and Halo: Reach where up to four players can fight against waves of attacking Covenant enemies.

  • If you play single-player Firefight, it’s just you against the attackers.
  • You can play co-operatively by using Social Matchmaking or by hosting your own Custom Firefight game and playing with the players you invited. They would be visible under “My Game Session” in the top right before starting the match.

Spartan Ops

Spartan Ops is a game mode in Halo 4 where up to four players can work as a team to perform various objectives while using their customized Halo 4 loadouts. You can play Spartan Ops co-op, but you can play it single-player instead if you prefer.

Why Don’t I Have Access to Halo 3: ODST or Halo: Reach in My Halo: The Master Chief Collection?

Halo 3: ODST and Halo: Reach were not released alongside the original Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC) in 2014. Because they were released later and can be bought separately, there are some situations where someone can own Halo: MCC but not have access to the campaigns and firefight mode for Halo 3: ODST or Halo: Reach.

Some Xbox Game Pass players have full access to every Halo game within Halo: MCC while they are subscribed. You can check the Halo: The Master Chief Collection page on the Xbox Store to see which Game Passes it’s available on.

For those who purchased Halo: MCC separately, here’s the full breakdown:

Halo 3: ODST

The Xbox Network & Networking Issues

If you are having networking-related issues with the Xbox network, please first check the status of Xbox Live services.

If you are still unable to connect, check Troubleshoot your Xbox network connection at Xbox Support.

If you are having internet trouble that is not specific to Halo or the Xbox network, sometimes power cycling can fix the issue. To power cycle:

  • Unplug the power cable to your modem for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
  • Unplug the power cable to your router for 30 seconds, then plug it back in.
  • Hold the power button down on your Xbox One console for 10 seconds. If you have tried everything above and you still have networking-related issues with the Xbox network, please submit a ticket.

Halo 2 Anniversary

Audio Issues When Watching Halo 2 Classic Cinematics in Halo: The Master Chief Collection

If you are experiencing low or no audio while watching cinematics in Halo 2 Classic mode, it is possible your Effects Volume & Game Music Volume is low or set to 0.

To fix:

  • Log into your game using your Gamertag
  • Navigate to Options & Career
  • Navigate to Settings
  • Adjust the settings for Effects Volume and Game Music Volume as desired

Halo 2: Anniversary Known Issues

The following are active issues for Halo 2: Anniversary as of 7/12/2023 in build 1.3232.0.

Campaign

  • New - Players in online co-op sessions may be booted to the main menu and receive “Connection Interrupted” errors in the following scenarios:
    • When one player triggers a checkpoint while driving a Scorpion and another player is driving a different vehicle.
    • When skipping the opening cutscene in the mission Outskirts.
    • When playing a Campaign Playlist.

    • Cutscene subtitles are still available for all non-English languages.

  • Cinematic audio for Halo 2 and Halo 2: Anniversary is affected by different audio options.

  • When the Scarab Skull is enabled, gunfire sound effects are missing from multiple weapons.

Halo 2: Anniversary Multiplayer

  • If the New Skins setting is set to Disabled, players who have new armor pieces equipped will appear to have low resolution default armor.
  • Any camera turning caused by a view angle restriction while in a vehicle passenger seat will stutter above 60 FPS.
  • Some pixilation is visible on shadows.
  • Performance lowers during games of 3 Plots.
  • Some maps have areas where texture resolution appears lower-than-expected.
  • When looking at the fan on Stonetown, the framerate sometimes drops to 45 frames per second.
  • Lighting is inconsistent between Elite and Spartan armor.
  • The Hoplite armor is missing a rear armor piece in gameplay.
  • When using “Any” or “Team” voice chat options and one player is speaking, voice chat icons appear over all friendly players instead of only the person speaking.

Halo 2: Classic Multiplayer

  • In game variants with time-based scoring (such as Oddball or King of the Hill), the timer in the bottom right corner of the screen may overlap the score’s progress bar.
  • Hit registration is not in parity with the original game.
  • The respawn timer is hidden by the territory capture meter.
  • Super bouncing does not mirror legacy behavior.

Forge

  • The Trait Zone Properties options cannot be changed when clicked with a mouse, however, the arrow keys on a keyboard will work as expected.
  • Halo 2: Anniversary Multiplayer films are capped at 60 FPS even when the unlimited framerate option is enabled.

Settings

  • New - The Select Next Grenades action does not function with any of the established layouts for Halo 2: Anniversary or when bound to a selected button via Custom layout with any of the controller layout presets for Halo 2: Anniversary.

Extras

  • The “Another Day at the Beach” and “Friend or Foe” cinematics in the Extras menu do not have subtitles.
  • In the Extras menu, all dialogue in cutscenes for Halo 2 Anniversary is aligned to the left audio channel.

Halo 3: ODST

Halo 3: ODST Firefight Achievements Are Not Included in Halo: The Master Chief Collection

The Xbox 360 Achievements for Halo 3: ODST’s Firefight mode are not included in Halo: The Master Chief Collection.

While not containing Xbox 360 Achievements, players can play challenging survival scenarios that offer many opportunities for strategic teamwork and replay ability. Weekly and monthly challenges reward players for completing specific objectives.

If you would like to provide feedback about Halo 3: ODST, visit the Halo Discord server. This is the best place to share ideas for what you want to see changed, improved, or done differently.

Halo 3: ODST Known Issues

The following are active issues for Halo 3: ODST as of 7/12/2023 in build 1.3232.0.

User Interface (UI)

  • Stats and Medals earned in Halo 3: ODST’s Firefight mode are not uniquely identified in the Options & Career menus.

Gameplay

  • Shadows cast on characters, enemies, and vehicles may appear very dark during gameplay.
  • Splitscreen players on 5.1 Surround Sound may encounter issues with audio transitions after an audio log is complete.
  • Single shot weapons, such as the Automag or Covenent Carbine, recoil more aggressively than in the original game.
  • Players who are at non-16:9 aspect ratios, extended Field of View (FOV), and/or centered crosshair will occasionally see through the player’s character model.

Firefight

  • New - When joining a Firefight match via the Custom Game Browser, there is no message in Spectator mode informing players that they will join once the current wave of enemies has been eliminated.
  • Brute AI can become stuck when trying to vault over railing or low walls.
    • We have made several improvements based on feedback from our recent Halo 3: ODST flight, but are still nailing down other places this issue occurs.
    • Please submit a ticket with Halo Support if you encounter this and include media, replication steps, and additional details about when or how this was encountered to provide our developers an in-depth view of the issue.
  • Player grenades appear to teleport and explode offset from initial landing spot.

Campaign

  • When playing with an ultrawide aspect ratio above 21:9 on PC, letterboxing along the top and bottom of the screen cuts off cutscenes.
  • Mission progress resets to the beginning of the mission when selecting Resume Campaign after switching between an Xbox One console and an Xbox Series X|S console.
  • Player loses Audio Log collection progress after death when working on “Record Store Owner” achievement.

Theater

  • Films from the mission “Mombasa Streets” will sometimes show an inaccurate name and preview image in menus and load screens.
  • On Xbox One, Flying Camera Settings do not apply to Theater controls.

“Record Store Owner” Achievement Won’t Unlock for Halo 3: ODST in Halo: The Master Chief Collection (MCC)

Some players have reported that the achievement “Record Store Owner” for Halo 3: ODST (within MCC) does not unlock unless all audio logs are collected in order.

We recommend making sure you collect each log in order. You will see the list of the ones you have found in-game.

If you missed one, you will want to re-play the campaign on co-op and collect all the audio logs again, making sure to grab the one you missed before. This should trigger the achievement.
