Halo: Campaign Evolved Player Guide

Halo: Campaign Evolved is an expanded remake of the 2001 Halo: Combat Evolved campaign, featuring high-definition visuals, a remastered soundtrack, and newly recorded dialogue from returning cast members. The campaign includes updated level design, refined controls, expanded gameplay, and three new prequel missions in Operation: Meteorite.

This player guide brings together key information and resources to help you understand the game’s features and modes, while also linking to more detailed guidance on things like PC resources or purchasing the game, providing a central place to find what you need and get the most out of Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Playing Together

A photograph of a large display showing a split-screen gameplay view. Two players are visible, seated in front of the screen.

Halo: Campaign Evolved supports cross-platform Co-Op on PC, XBOX Series X|S, and PlayStation®5, with shared progression across all supported platforms. Split-screen is also available for up to two players on console.

For more information on playing together and adding friends across platforms, check out Co-op in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Operation: Meteorite

A picture from a game cinematic of Sergeant Johnson and Master Chief aboard a covenant research ship in Operation: Meteorite.

Operation: Meteorite is a three-mission bonus campaign set one year before the events of Halo: Campaign Evolved. In this campaign, Master Chief and Sergeant Major Avery Johnson board a Covenant research ship to recover navigation data. It includes new environments, a new Covenant faction, and missions that extend into space.

Operation: Meteorite is included in all editions of Halo: Campaign Evolved and is available immediately.

Campaign Remix

An in-game capture of Flood forms present on The Silent Cartographer mission with a green fog, caused by active Campaign Remix skulls.

Campaign Remix is an unlockable mode that modifies missions by applying different Skull combinations and encounter variations. These changes can significantly alter combat scenarios, creating unique gameplay each time a mission is replayed.

To learn how to unlock Campaign Remix and view a detailed breakdown of the enabled Skulls and gameplay mechanics, read our guide on Halo: Campaign Evolved Campaign Remix.

Expanded Sandbox

An in-game capture of an armory with assorted Plasma Rifles, Brute Plasma Rifles, and Plasma Grenades.

Halo: Campaign Evolved adds additional weapons to the campaign sandbox, alongside the classic weapons from the original game. Vehicle gameplay is also expanded, including a fourth Warthog seat, and new capabilities like piloting Wraith tanks and hijacking vehicles.

For a complete breakdown of weapons and vehicles, read our Weapons & Vehicles overview.

Collectibles

An in-game capture of a hidden terminal in a Forerunner hallway.

39 skulls and 13 terminals are hidden throughout the game world. These items reward exploration, provide additional insight into the story and setting, and unlock additional modes to play.

A detailed list of the items and rewards is available here: Collectibles in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

LASO

LASO, meaning Legendary-All-Skulls-On, is a campaign challenge that combines Legendary difficulty with Skulls enabled. With 17 Skulls active at once, it is the most challenging mode in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

For details on how to unlock LASO, a list of the active Skulls, their effects, and related achievements you can earn, visit our guide on LASO in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Game Editions

Halo: Campaign Evolved is available in multiple editions, with some offering bonuses such as customization packs and digital extras.

To compare editions and understand what’s included in each, our Halo: Campaign Evolved Editions guide will walk through each edition and inclusions.

Some editions include the Digital Story & Art Collection app. To learn more about what the app includes and how it works, see our overview of the Halo: Campaign Evolved Digital Story & Art Collection.

PC Specifications & Drivers

A wide range of PC hardware configurations are supported, allowing you to adjust settings for a smooth and stable experience.

For a one-stop guide on setting up your game for the best performance and visuals possible, follow our instructions for Optimizing your PC Experience in Halo: Campaign Evolved.

To ensure your PC and drivers are ready to run the game, review the PC Specifications & Drivers for Halo: Campaign Evolved.

Safety & Accessibility

Halo: Campaign Evolved includes accessibility and safety designed to let you tailor your experience, both in-game and across platforms.

Check out Accessibility in Halo: Campaign Evolved to adjust gameplay settings such as controls, visuals, and audio.

For information about managing interactions, communication, and reporting misbehavior, Safety Features in Halo: Campaign Evolved provides an overview of how to control your experience. The article includes links to platform safety resources for XBOX, PlayStation®, Steam, and Microsoft to help you manage your experience.

How to Change the Field of View (FOV) Setting in Halo Infinite

Increasing the Field-of-View (FOV) setting allows players to see more of the battlefield and surroundings while playing. This may reduce a potential feeling of “tunnel vision” or motion sickness that some players experience.

To change the FOV setting in Halo Infinite:

  • The first step depends on your platform:
    • PC: From any menu while not in a match, press the ESC key on your keyboard until you’ve reached the Control Panel menu.
    • Xbox console: From any menu while not in a match, press the Menu button on your Xbox controller (the one with three horizontal lines near the middle of your controller) to bring up the Control Panel menu.
  • Choose Settings
  • Select the Video tab along the top of the menu
  • Under the Display section, see the slider labeled Field of View
  • Adjust the slider to your desired setting. The default is 78°. To widen your field of view, raise this number
  • When you exit the menu, your setting will save

Additional tips

  • You may pause and adjust FOV during gameplay
  • At FOV settings higher than the default (78°), looking straight down will make your character’s legs no longer visible to you. This will not affect gameplay
  • Higher FOV settings may reduce frames per second (FPS)

How to Customize Your Spartan, Guns, Vehicles, and Personal AI in Halo Infinite

In Halo Infinite you can customize the appearance of your Spartan in multiplayer. Customizations do not apply to Campaign. Customization options (cosmetics) can be earned through gameplay, challenges and events, or be purchased.

All customizations in Halo Infinite are cosmetic and do not provide in-game advantages.

Customizations are equipped through the Customization menu. The Customization menu contains the Armor Hall, Weapons Bench, Vehicle Bay, Body & AI, and Spartan ID menus.

When applying customizations in any of these menus, make sure to Equip each item after inspecting it. Inspecting an item will show you how a locked item can be earned.

Armor Hall

In the Armor Hall, select an unlocked Armor Core. These Armor Cores can be customized further by inspecting and modifying armor parts such as:

  • Armor Kit (a set of unique customizations)
  • Coating
  • Helmet
  • Visor
  • Chest
  • Shoulder pads
  • Gloves
  • Wrist
  • Utility
  • Knee pads
  • Emblem
  • Emblem palette
  • Armor effects Some customizations can only be used on specific Armor Cores.

Weapons Bench

From the Weapons Bench, choose an unlocked Weapon Cores and customize the:

  • Weapons Kit (a set of unique customizations)
  • Coating
  • Model
  • Charm
  • Emblem
  • Emblem palette
  • Kill effects Some customizations can only be used on specific Weapon Cores.

Vehicle Bay

From the Vehicle Bay, choose an unlocked Vehicle Core and customize the:

  • Coating
  • Model
  • Emblem
  • Emblem palette Some customizations can only be used on specific Vehicle Cores.

Body & AI

From Body & AI, players can choose:

  • Spartan’s body type
  • Prosthetic arm and leg options
  • Personal AI model
  • Personal AI color Spartan body types and prosthetic options are all unlocked by default.

Personal AI model determines what the Personal AI sounds like and looks like in-game.

Spartan ID

From Spartan ID, players can customize parts of how their Spartan is presented in lobbies, during gameplay, in their profile, and when others select their gamertag in Social menus. These options include:

  • Service Tag
    • 1-4 characters. This appears next to your gamertag
  • Voice
  • Nameplate
  • Nameplate palette
  • Nameplate backdrop
  • Stance

How to Give Feedback about Halo Infinite and Discuss the Game

Please provide feedback about Halo Infinite on the Halo Discord server. This is the best place to share ideas for what you want to see changed, improved, or done differently.

Halo Support (where you are now) provides self-help information and is where you can submit tickets about in-game bugs and issues. The data from those tickets helps the developers find problems and prioritize fixes that have the biggest impact on players. Our processes are not designed to collect feedback or ideas.

If you would like more opportunities to share feedback, we strongly encourage you to join the Halo Insider Program and keep your Insider profile up to date.

How to Mute Players in Halo Infinite

How to mute individual players

You can mute players at any time during a multiplayer match. To do so, follow the steps below:

  • Open the multiplayer scoreboard.
    • On Keyboard/Mouse, press the Tab key.
    • On Controller, press the View button.
  • Press the button indicated by the menu prompt at the bottom of the screen to enable interactive mode. You will be unable to move or look around in-game after entering interactive mode.
    • If there is no button or key listed at the bottom of the screen, the Scoreboard Interact binding may not be set. Select the Controller or Keyboard/Mouse tab in the Settings menu, then scroll down to the Campaign Menu/Scoreboard section to change this binding.
  • From the scoreboard, navigate to the Gamertag of the player you wish to mute.
  • Press the corresponding button prompt at the bottom of the screen to mute the player.
  • Press the corresponding button prompt at the bottom of the screen to close interactive mode and return to gameplay. To determine if a player is muted or unmuted, open the multiplayer scoreboard and check the white speaker icon to the left of their Gamertag. Muted players will have a diagonal line striking through their speaker icon. You cannot unmute a player that has muted themselves.

Global mute and chat settings

The default mute and chat settings can be modified in the Settings menu via the Audio tab.

  • From the main menu, open the Settings menu.
    • The default bindings are ESC/F1 on keyboard or the Menu button on controller.
  • Select Settings.
  • Go to the Audio tab.
  • Scroll down to Communication.
    • Voice chat mode allows you to enable your own settings, which includes Open Mic, Push-to-Talk, Disabled, and Toggle-to-Talk.
      • The button mapping for Push-to-Talk can be altered in the Keyboard/Mouse tab under Communication.
    • The Match Chat option sets whether you want to receive voice and text chat messages from other players.

How to Play Halo Infinite Multiplayer Online Using Matchmaking

Matchmaking is how Halo Infinite finds players you do not know and puts you in a game together. Multiplayer games can be a combination of people you do not know and members of your fireteam. To only play with friends and avoid matchmaking, select Custom Games.

  • From the main menu (Play), select Multiplayer
  • Choose a multiplayer playlist from the list
    • Playlists are collections of different multiplayer game modes
  • If you would like to play with friends, you can add them to your fireteam at this time
    • See How to Play Halo Infinite Multiplayer with friends for information.
  • Select Play. Wait times may vary but are usually under a few minutes
    • You may exit any time before your match is made. Quitting once matched or during a game is a bad experience for your teammates who are left unsupported. You will lose any stats/progress earned in the match and will be at risk of an automated or manual enforcement ban for abandoning a match.
    • Members of a fireteam will be placed in the same game together, unless there are limitations for that game mode If you’re having trouble loading into Multiplayer matches, please check Xbox Live status at Xbox Support.

How to Play Halo Infinite Multiplayer with Friends

There are many ways to play Halo Infinite with friends online using the Xbox network, such as competitive Multiplayer, Campaign mode via Network Co-Op, and building Forge maps. Halo Infinite also features cross-play, which allows you to play with friends on either PC or Xbox consoles.

How to Add Friends Using the Xbox Network

To play with friends online, you must first add them as a friend on your Xbox account. Visit How to add new Xbox friends | Xbox Support for detailed steps for adding friends.

How to Add Players to Your Fireteam

Once the person you would like to play with has been added as a friend on the Xbox network, you can now invite them to join your Fireteam in Halo Infinite.

To add players to your Fireteam, follow the steps below:

  • By default, press the Tab key on keyboard or the View button on controller to open the Social menu.
  • Switch to the Friends or Recent tab to view the list of Gamertags you can invite to your Fireteam.
  • You can use the Find Friends feature to help you locate and add your friends’ Gamertag to your friends list. This function only works for Xbox Friends and Xbox Gamertags.
    • On PC, you can press the G key (default keybinding) to add friends through Discord. This feature only works if Discord is installed on your PC.
  • Select the Gamertag you would like to invite to your Fireteam.
  • In the Player Options menu that pops up, select Invite.
  • If the player accepts your invitation, they will be added to your Fireteam and will appear under the Fireteam tab. The maximum Fireteam size differs depending on the selected mode. In Matchmaking, Fireteam sizes are based on the selected playlist. Whereas in Custom Games, you can manually change how many players can join your Fireteam. This allows you to have a Fireteam size of up to 24 players regardless of the selected mode. The chart below shows how many players can be invited into a Fireteam for each mode.

Mode

Maximum Fireteam Size

Arena (4v4) Matchmaking

4

BTB (12v12) Matchmaking

12

Custom Games

28*

Forge

8

Network Co-Op Campaign

4

*In Custom Games, the maximum number of players allowed in a Fireteam is 28, but only 24 players can play in a match. The remaining 4 players play as Observers, who are able to view the match from the perspective of any player they select.

How to Create an Open Lobby for Others to Join

You can create an Open/Public lobby to play with other players who you have not added to your friends list.

Create an Open/Public Fireteam Lobby:

  • Press the View button to open the Social screen.

  • Above your name, highlight and select the In Menus option.

  • Change the Privacy setting to Public.

  • Select Back then then Close to return to the Main Menu. Create an Open/Pubic Custom Game lobby:

  • From the Main Menu open Custom Games.

  • Select Create match and create a match to your preferences.

  • Open Lobby Options and change Visibility to Public. Join an Open/Public Lobby:

  • Add the person with the open lobby to your Xbox Friends list.

  • To join the open lobby, press the View button and navigate to the Friends tab.

  • Highlight the friend who has the open lobby and select their name to open the Player Options view.

  • Navigate down and select the Join option.

How to Use Split-Screen to Play Halo Infinite Multiplayer

Multiplayer can also be experienced via split-screen. Split-screen is the term for when 2 or more people are playing on the same Xbox console using the same screen. Local split-screen is exclusively accessible on Xbox consoles and applies only to competitive Multiplayer.

On Xbox One consoles, split-screen supports 2 players.

On Xbox Series X|S consoles, the number of players that can use split-screen varies depending on the selected mode. This chart shows how many players can play split-screen for each mode.

Mode

Maximum Split-Screen Players

Arena (4v4) Matchmaking

4

BTB (12v12) Matchmaking

2

Local Custom Games (12v12)*

4

  • Matches up to 24 players (12v12) on a Local Area Network. At max capacity, (24 players) this would equate to 6 consoles with each having a 4 player split-screen.

To play local multiplayer with your friends using split-screen, follow the steps below:

  • Turn on a second Xbox controller synced to your Xbox console.
  • Log into a second Xbox account using the second controller.
    • You cannot use Xbox guest accounts in Halo Infinite multiplayer.
  • The second player will be added to your Fireteam locally and join you in any multiplayer mode that supports split-screen, as described above.

How to Play Halo: Campaign Evolved Offline

This article covers how to play Halo: Campaign Evolved offline.

On Steam and PlayStation®, you must use an internet connection to perform the initial account linking process. After the initial link is complete, the steps below will allow you to play without an internet connection.

Some platforms require additional platform-specific settings to be configured before offline play is available. Select your platform below for setup instructions for playing Halo: Campaign Evolved offline.

XBOX

Offline play on XBOX is available for up to 2 players, including single-player and local split-screen co-op on a single console. Each player must sign in with a unique Microsoft account and Gamertag.

Please note that you must be connected to the internet the first time you set up your XBOX. After setup is complete and your profile has been added, you can play offline.

To learn more about XBOX offline play, visit Using Your XBOX Console Offline | XBOX Support.

PlayStation®5

Offline play on PlayStation®5 is available for up to 2 players, including single-player and local split-screen co-op on a single console.

For co-op, each player must have a PlayStation™Network account linked to a Microsoft account with an XBOX gamertag. If a player attempts to sign in with a Microsoft account that does not yet have an XBOX gamertag, they will receive an error message.

One-Time Online Setup

An internet connection is required the first time you launch the game to link your PlayStation™Network account to your Microsoft account. After your account has been linked, you can play the game offline.

For instructions and additional information on the account linking process, visit our Account Linking & Unlinking in Halo: Campaign Evolved article.

How to Enable Offline Play

Before playing offline, you must enable Console Sharing and Offline Play on the PlayStation®5 console.

  • Sign in to the PlayStation™Network account that owns the game.
  • Open the PlayStation®5 console Settings.
  • Select Users and Accounts.
  • Select Other.
  • Select Console Sharing and Offline Play. To learn more about PlayStation® offline play, visit How to Turn on PS5 Console Sharing and Offline Play | PlayStation Support.

Microsoft Store/XBOX App PC

Offline play on the Microsoft Store or XBOX App for PC is available for single-player gameplay.

Please note that an internet connection is required the first time you launch Halo: Campaign Evolved. Before you start the game, sign into the Microsoft Store and XBOX app with the account that purchased the title, then launch the game at least once while connected to the internet.

How to Enable Offline Play

Before playing offline, you must enable Offline permissions in the Microsoft Store app.

  • Open the Microsoft Store app.
  • Select your profile icon at the top.
  • Select Store Settings.
  • Toggle on Offline permissions. To learn more about Windows PC offline play, visit Play games in offline mode on Windows | XBOX Support.

Steam

Offline play on Steam is available for single-player campaigns. A Steam account linked to a Microsoft account with an XBOX gamertag is required.

One-Time Online Setup

An internet connection is required the first time you launch the game to link your Steam account to your Microsoft account. After your account has been linked, you can play the game offline. For instructions and additional information on the account linking process, visit our Account Linking & Unlinking in Halo: Campaign Evolved article.

To learn more about Steam offline play, visit Offline Mode | Steam Support.

If you encounter issues playing offline, linking accounts, or anything else related to offline play in Halo: Campaign Evolved, submit a ticket to Halo Support.

How to Purchase Virtual Currency for Halo Infinite on Halo Waypoint

This article details how to purchase virtual currency for Halo Infinite, also known as Credits, on the Halo Waypoint website.

Halo Waypoint serves as the online player hub for all Halo-related news, gameplay statistics, and more. The Halo Infinite section of Halo Waypoint allows players to review their Battle Pass progression, view or update their virtual currency balance, and purchase Shop items and Battle Passes with their available virtual currency.

Various accessibility features and settings are available to ensure the virtual currency purchase process is comfortable and convenient for all players.

Purchasing virtual currency (Credits) on Halo Waypoint

Use the steps below to purchase virtual currency for Halo Infinite via the Halo Waypoint website.

  • Navigate to HaloWaypoint.com within a web browser.
  • On the Halo Waypoint home page, click on the black square labeled “SIGN IN” in the top right corner of the page.
  • Clicking the Sign In button will load the Xbox network login page. Enter your account’s associated email address, phone number, or Skype account name. Depending on your account’s selected security settings, enter your account password and/or complete the two-factor authentication (2FA) prompts.
    • If you do not have an Xbox or Microsoft account, review the supporting documentation then create an account on Xbox.com: Account with Xbox.
  • Completing the Xbox sign-in process will redirect back to the Halo Waypoint home page and the Sign In button in the top right corner of the window will now display the signed-in account’s profile picture.
  • Click on the account’s profile picture in the top right corner of the window and select “Service Records” from the dropdown menu.
  • On the Service Records page, select the “Go to Service Record” button within the Halo Infinite section.
  • On the Halo Infinite Service Record page, click on the “STORE” tab below the “HALO INFINITE” header near the top of the page.
  • Select the secondary tab labeled “BUY CREDITS” below the Store tab button.
  • Identify the Credits bundle you would like to purchase then select the “BUY” button within that bundle’s tile.
  • Clicking the Buy button will redirect players to the Xbox.com store listing for their selected bundle. Complete the Xbox.com purchase flow to buy the selected virtual currency bundle.

Purchasing Halo Infinite Battle Passes and Operation Passes on Halo Waypoint

Use the steps below to purchase Halo Infinite Battle Passes and Operation Passes via the Halo Waypoint website.

  • Navigate to HaloWaypoint.com within a web browser.
  • On the Halo Waypoint home page, click on the black square labeled “SIGN IN” in the top right corner of the page.
  • Clicking the Sign In button will load the Xbox network login page. Enter your account’s associated email address, phone number, or Skype account name. Depending on your account’s selected security settings, enter your account password and/or complete the two-factor authentication (2FA) prompts.
    • If you do not have an Xbox or Microsoft account, review the supporting documentation then create an account on Xbox.com: Account with Xbox.
  • Completing the Xbox sign-in process will redirect back to the Halo Waypoint home page and the Sign In button in the top right corner of the window will now display the signed-in account’s profile picture.
  • Click on the account’s profile picture in the top right corner of the window and select “Service Records” from the dropdown menu.
  • On the Service Records page, select the “Go to Service Record” button within the Halo Infinite section.
  • When opened, the Halo Infinite Service Record page displays the “PROGRESS” tab and the “SUMMARY” secondary tab. Within the Summary secondary tab, click on the “CHANGE BATTLEPASS” button within the Battle Pass tile.
  • Within the resulting “EQUIP A BATTLE PASS” window, identify and locate the Battle Pass or Operation Pass you would like to purchase. Once located, select the “BUY” button to view the available purchase offers.
  • Select either the Premium Battle Pass offer or the Premium Pass Bundle offer in the resulting menu.
  • Review and confirm the purchase in the “BUY CONFIRMATION” window to spend the required Credits and obtain the offer’s items.

Purchasing Halo Infinite Shop Items on Halo Waypoint

Use the steps below to purchase Halo Infinite Shop items, such as cosmetic customization items, XP Boosts, and Challenge Swaps, via the Halo Waypoint website.

  • Navigate to HaloWaypoint.com within a web browser.
  • On the Halo Waypoint home page, click on the black square labeled “SIGN IN” in the top right corner of the page.
  • Clicking the Sign In button will load the Xbox network login page. Enter your account’s associated email address, phone number, or Skype account name. Depending on your account’s selected security settings, enter your account password and/or complete the two-factor authentication (2FA) prompts.
    • If you do not have an Xbox or Microsoft account, review the supporting documentation then create an account on Xbox.com: Account with Xbox.
  • Completing the Xbox sign-in process will redirect back to the Halo Waypoint home page and the Sign In button in the top right corner of the window will now display the signed-in account’s profile picture.
  • Click on the account’s profile picture in the top right corner of the window and select “Service Records” from the dropdown menu.
  • On the Service Records page, select the “Go to Service Record” button within the Halo Infinite section.
  • On the Halo Infinite Service Record page, click on the “STORE” tab below the “HALO INFINITE” header near the top of the page.
  • When opened, the Halo Infinite Store tab displays the “FEATURED” secondary tab. Identify the Store bundle you would like to purchase.
    • The “EXCHANGE” tile in the Featured tab leads to a second storefront which features cosmetic customization items that can be purchased with Spartan Points, a virtual currency earned by completing gameplay challenges in Halo Infinite multiplayer matchmaking.
  • Once you have identified the Store or Exchange bundle you would like to purchase, select the “Buy” button within its tile to begin the purchase process.
    • If no “Buy” button is visible, the signed-in account does not have enough virtual currency to complete the purchase.
  • Review and confirm the purchase in the “BUY CONFIRMATION” window to spend the required Credits and obtain the bundle’s items.

Additional Information

To learn more about the accessibility of Halo Waypoint’s purchase processes, please visit Microsoft’s Accessibility Conformance Reports portal and search for “Halo Waypoint” to view supporting documentation.

How to Resolve PC File Corruption Error for Halo Infinite

There are rare instances where players are unable to access Halo Infinite on PC due to file corruption. This corruption may be introduced when first installing Halo Infinite or when installing a game update.

This issue may appear in a variety of ways:

  • Halo Infinite crashes without any error messaging.
  • Halo Infinite appears to freeze and a Windows error message referring to “Damaged media” or “module is damaged” appears.
  • Halo Infinite stops responding, and Windows prompts you to restart or exit the game.

Steam

If you downloaded Halo Infinite via Steam, it’s possible that the game files were corrupted during the installation or update process. This issue may be resolved by verifying the integrity of the local game files. Follow the steps below:

  • From your Steam library, right click on Halo Infinite from your games list.
  • Select Properties via the dropdown menu.
  • While in the Properties menu, select Local Files.
  • Click on Verify Integrity of Local Game Files.
  • Once the process is complete, restart your PC.

Microsoft Store

If you downloaded Halo Infinite from the Microsoft store, you may be able to repair the game files using Windows system settings. Follow the steps below:

  • Open the Start menu on Windows by clicking on the task bar’s Windows icon or by pressing the Windows key on the keyboard.
  • Type “Apps & Features” into the Search bar then press the Enter key.
  • In the Apps & Features Settings window, scroll down and select Halo Infinite.
  • Select Advanced Options.
  • Scroll down and select Repair. If the error is persisting after using the Repair option, follow Steps 1-4 above, then select Uninstall instead of Repair. Once you have uninstalled Halo Infinite, you can re-download it using the steps in our installation guide.

Xbox App

  • In Xbox App, select Halo Infinite in your library.
  • Click the menu “More actions for Halo Infinite”, select the option “Manage”.
  • Select the “Files” tab and then click “Verify and Repair” button.
  • After the process is completed, launch the game and check if the issue is still occurring.

How to Take a Clip or Screenshot and Share It in Halo Infinite

There are two main ways to capture moments in Halo Infinite. Capturing through the built-in features of Xbox and through Theater mode. In Theater mode players can watch multiplayer films they have bookmarked, and watch films generated from their match history.

Halo Infinite Theater

Go to the Community menu to find Theater. Through the Community menu you can view match replays, bookmark your favorites, and watch other people’s popular replays.

If you would like to preserve your Theater films long term, we recommend you save them using Xbox capture or another digital video recording tool. Substantial updates, such as moving from Beta to full release, can reset your history and bookmarks or result in some films becoming deprecated due to changes in game content.

Xbox capture

Capture on Xbox consoles records up to 10 minutes on internal storage or up to 1 hour on external storage. Players can also record the last 30 seconds of gameplay, capturing video of an event after it happened. Both of these options are accessed via the Xbox button.

The Xbox Game Bar app handles game captures on Windows 10 and later devices. By default:

  • Win button + Alt+PrintScreen: Take a screenshot of your game.

  • Win button + Alt + G: Record the last few moments of game play. For a step-by-step guide, please go to Xbox Support’s Capture game clips and screenshots article. It covers the common questions, including how to:

  • Capture a clip or screenshot of something that just happened on Xbox One or Xbox Series X|S

  • Record a clip of what’s going to happen next

  • Use Xbox Game Bar on a PC to capture game clips

  • Capture 4K HDR game clips and screenshots Xbox Support’s Share clips and screenshots article contains information about how to share your captures on console, from your phone and from Windows.

If you have any problems, please go to Xbox Support. Halo Support cannot help with Xbox-level issues.

How to Use Challenge Swaps and XP Boosts in Halo Infinite

There are three main types of consumable items in Halo Infinite: XP Boosts, Challenge Swaps, and XP Grants. Each is activated and used (consumed) to provide a unique benefit. XP Boosts and Challenge Swaps can be acquired through Battle Pass progress or purchased in the Shop.

XP Boosts

XP Boosts can be consumed to grant double XP toward Battle Pass progress for the next 60 minutes.

To consume an XP Boost:

  • From the main menu, open the Battle Pass menu by pressing R on a keyboard or Y on an Xbox Controller.
  • Within the Battle Pass menu, open the Boosts menu by pressing R on a keyboard or Y on an Xbox Controller.
  • Select “Double XP Boost” from the options and confirm your choice.

Challenge Swap

Challenge Swaps can be consumed to switch out a currently active Weekly Challenge for a random new one. All progress on a current Challenge is lost if a Challenge Swap is used to get a new challenge.

To consume a Challenge Swap:

  • From the main menu, open the Battle Pass menu by pressing R on a keyboard or Y on an Xbox Controller.
  • Switch to the Challenges tab by pressing E on a keyboard or Right Bumper on an Xbox Controller.
  • Select the Challenge Swap icon to the left of the Challenge you want to switch out. The icon looks like two rotating arrows:
  • Confirm your choice by selecting “Swap.”

XP Grant

XP Grants can be consumed to grant a flat XP reward toward Battle Pass progress.

To consume an XP Grant:

  • From the main menu, open the Battle Pass menu by pressing R on a keyboard or Y on an Xbox Controller.
  • Within the Battle Pass menu, open the Boosts menu by pressing R on a keyboard or Y on an Xbox Controller.
  • Select “XP Grant” from the options and confirm your choice.

How to Use the Mark System in Halo Infinite

The Mark system helps players quickly communicate with teammates. Marking can also be called pinging a spot.

To mark a spot:

  • Put what you would like to mark in your crosshairs
  • Press X on a Keyboard or Up on the directional pad on an Xbox Controller Marked spots appear on teammates’ screens with information about the target. The symbol and color of the mark depend on what was marked. Marked information also appears in the Event Feed at the bottom left of the screen.

Marking objects does not make the object yours. A marked weapon, equipment, or vehicle can still be taken and used by an enemy.

Marker types

Locations

Marking the ground will call out the location on the map. For example, pinging the center hallway on the map Live Fire creates a mark for Hallway.

Weapons, Equipment, and Vehicles

Marking a weapon rack, power weapon, equipment, or vehicle on the map will share the name of the weapon or equipment and call out the location on the map.

Honk the horn of your vehicle (Right Trigger by default) to request additional passengers.

Enemies

Marking an enemy will create a red exclamation point marker on teammates’ screens and call out the location on the map.

LASO in Halo: Campaign Evolved

This article provides an overview of LASO (Legendary All Skulls On) mode, including the skulls required to unlock the mode and the achievements available for completing it.

What is LASO?

LASO stands for Legendary-All-Skulls-On, meaning Legendary difficulty with all skulls enabled. Skulls are gameplay modifiers that can affect enemy behavior, player attributes, and other gameplay elements. This mode is also commonly referred to as Mythic difficulty.

In earlier Halo titles with fewer skulls, LASO was a community-driven challenge without official rewards or achievements. As more skulls were added across the franchise, “All Skulls On” came to refer to a defined set of skulls rather than every skull available.

For the complete list of skulls in Halo: Campaign Evolved, visit our Collectibles guide.

How to Find Skulls

An in-game capture of a hidden skull, spotlighted by sunlight, inside of a cave.

Each mission contains 3 hidden skulls, for a total of 39 skulls hidden across Halo: Campaign Evolved. As players move near a skull, it emits a subtle ambient audio cue that indicates its location and gets louder as you close in on it.

All skulls can be collected using the Interact/Reload action. By default, this action is mapped to the X button (XBOX), Square button (PlayStation®), and E key (keyboard).

Unlocking LASO

In Halo: Campaign Evolved, LASO uses 17 specific skulls. These skulls must be discovered in the campaign before LASO mode becomes available. Once you discover the 17 skulls, the mode becomes available in the various Campaign and Campaign Remix menus.

An enlarged in-game Campaign Remix mode selection screen, featuring the unlocked “PLAY LASO” option.

Below is the list of the 17 LASO-specific skulls:

  • Iron- Dying in co-op resets you to your last checkpoint, dying while solo restarts the level.
  • Black Eye- Your shields will only recharge when you melee enemies.
  • Fog- Motion Tracker is disabled.
  • Famine- Weapons dropped by enemies contain half the ammo.
  • Thunderstorm- Upgrades the rank of most enemies.
  • Mythic- Enemies have increased health.
  • Grunt Birthday Party- Grunt headshots produce legendary celebrations.
  • IWHBYD- Rare dialogue becomes more common.
  • Boom- Explosion radius is increased by 2x.
  • Eye Patch- All auto-aim is disabled for all weapons.
  • Grunt Funeral- Grunts die in a blaze of plasma.
  • Malfunction- Upon respawn a random element of your HUD no longer appears.
  • That’s just… Wrong- Enemies have increased awareness of the player.
  • Speed Limit- Take your time, enjoy the sights! Disables sprint.
  • Pop- Shooting Flood in their weak point causes them to explode.
  • Temperamental- Allies will attack the player more quickly if the player kills a friendly.
  • Johnny Ammo Seed- When reloading, you lose the ammo remaining in the discarded clip. All 17 Skulls remain active for the entire LASO playthrough.

Because multiple gameplay modifiers are enabled at once, several core mechanics function differently than in standard Campaign play. For example, shields will not recharge until players melee an enemy and deaths will result in reverting to the last checkpoint in co-op, or restarting the entire level when solo. Players must approach each encounter with greater care and intent.

Achievements

Complete the Campaign with LASO enabled to earn the following rewards, depending on your platform:

  • XBOX: MYTHIC achievement worth 50 Gamerscore.
  • Steam: MYTHIC achievement on your Steam profile.
  • PlayStation®: MYTHIC Gold trophy. Please note that using difficulty modifiers will prevent these rewards from unlocking. For more information on difficulty modifiers, visit our Difficulty Settings & Modifiers guide.

If you do not see your achievements after completing a LASO playthrough, visit our Halo: Campaign Evolved Achievement Troubleshooting article for steps that may help resolve the issue.

Recommended Competitive Settings for Halo Infinite

This article contains the recommended Halo Infinite settings and related commentary from the Competitive Insights Team (CIT) at Halo Studios. The Competitive Insights Team helps ensure the quality of our games meet the needs of the high-skill and competitive players and are actively involved in the development process. Their recommended settings have been tested and reviewed as the most ideal setting configuration for players to perform at the highest level.

Note: Before implementing any of these settings on your PC, review the “PC hardware specs and drivers for Halo Infinite” article to ensure your system meets the minimum requirements. Additionally, CIT recommends using these settings as a baseline and adjusting further as needed: “While these settings may seem perfect for one player, they may not be for another. Use your own discretion based on your player feel and hardware capabilities.”

The above infographic outlines the required hardware specifications for the different graphics quality presets in Halo Infinite. Click the image to view it at its full resolution.

PC Hardware Specifications (text version)

Low (Minimum Requirements)

OS: Windows 10 RS5 x64 1809 (October 2018 update)

CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 1600 or Intel i5-4440

GPU: AMD RX 570 or Nvidia GTX 1050 Ti

VRAM: 4+ GB

RAM: 8+ GB

SSD: 50+ GB

Medium

OS: Windows 10 19H2 x64 1909 (November 2019 update)

CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 2600 or Intel i5-9500

GPU: AMD RX 5500 XT (8GB) or Nvidia GTX 1660 (6GB)

VRAM: 6+ GB

RAM: 8+ GB

SSD: 50+ GB

High (Recommended)

OS: Windows 10 19H2 x64 1909 (November 2019 update)

CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 3700X or Intel i7-9700k

GPU: AMD RX 5700XT or Nvidia RTX 2070

VRAM: 8+ GB

RAM: 16+ GB

SSD: 50+ GB

Ultra

OS: Windows 10 19H2 x64 1909 (November 2019 update)

CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X or Intel i9-11900k

GPU: AMD 6800 XT or Nvidia RTX 3080

VRAM: 10+ GB

RAM: 16+ GB

SSD: 50+GB

Controller/Mouse and Keyboard

  • Vibration: Disabled CIT commentary: “[Only pertains to controller players] – The majority of ranked players prefer vibration disabled rather than enabled. This mainly stems from the use of headphones to determine where enemy damage sources are coming from instead of relying on controller vibration.”

  • Hold to Crouch: Enabled

  • Hold to Zoom: Disabled

  • Hold to Sprint: Disabled

  • Movement Assisted Steering: Disabled

  • Maintain Sprint: Enabled

  • Auto Clamber: Disabled

  • Step Jump: Enabled CIT commentary: “All sensitivity settings, controller layouts, mouse and keyboard binds are very subjective. We recommend using what is most comfortable and common for yourself. However, there are a few settings shown above that give yourself more autonomy with movement.”

Video

Global

The two screenshots above illustrate the difference between the default Field of View value of 78° and the recommended value of 100°. Click the image above to view it at its full resolution.

  • Field of View: 100° CIT commentary: “This Field of View is a great starting point. Adjust accordingly.”

  • Blur: 0%

  • Screen Shake: 0%

  • Exposure: 0%

  • Full Screen Effects: 0%

  • Speed Lines: Disabled

  • Sharpening: 60% CIT commentary: “While these settings do give players a heightened sense of immersion, some competitive players may find that adjusting these options will allow them to focus more on their gameplay.”

  • Brightness: Adjust to your preference CIT commentary: “Some players tend to increase their in-game screen brightness. To do so, navigate to the Video tab and use the Screen Calibration shortcut listed along the bottom of the screen. From there, it will take you to a screen to adjust your brightness. Generally speaking, players prefer a higher brightness setting to help with spotting enemies, details, and any other visual cues. We recommend starting at default 0 and adjust to your personal preference.”

The Brightness option can be found in the Screen Calibration menu, which can be found via the shortcut listed along the bottom of the Video tab in the Settings menu. By default, the shortcut is mapped to the R key on keyboard and the Y button on controller.

PC
  • Resolution Scale: 100%
  • Minimum Frame Rate: 120
  • Maximum Frame Rate: Unlimited CIT commentary: “Resolution Scale – If you are looking to increase your frame rate as much as possible, we recommend adjusting your resolution to the lowest setting that you’d be comfortable playing on. This is dependent on your hardware capabilities.”

Halo Support note: “When setting the Minimum Frame Rate to 120, the game will prioritize maintaining 120 frames per second and deprioritize its resolution. In other words, the resolution may drop to a point that it appears ‘blurry’ or ‘fuzzy’ during demanding gameplay. If this is occurring, you may want to select a lower Minimum Frame Rate value.”

  • VSync: Disabled CIT commentary: “While this will come down to personal preference, competitive players usually turn off VSync to allow their GPU to rendering at a higher frame rate.”

Halo Support note: “Disabling VSync may result in the image appearing to ‘tear’ or ‘split’ during gameplay. Enabling VSync may result in a hit to the game’s peak and average frame rate, but instances of the image splitting will be significantly reduced.”

  • Quality Preset: Low

  • Effects Quality: Medium

  • Animation Quality: Max

  • Simulation Quality: Ultra CIT commentary: “Setting your graphics quality preset to low will give your machine the highest performance capabilities. However, there are three adjustments within graphics that are recommended to fine tune your performance.”

  • Async Compute Halo Support note: “There is no one-size-fits-all recommendation for the Async Compute option. Enabling Async Compute increases your CPU overhead, meaning that your CPU will need to work harder. Depending on your PC configuration, enabling this option may result in either of the following scenarios:

  • If your PC’s performance is not bound by its CPU, enabling Async Compute may reduce your GPU overhead and result in higher performance.

  • If your PC’s performance is bound by its CPU, enabling Async Compute will likely result in lower performance.”

Xbox consoles
  • Target Frame Rate: 60 or 120 CIT commentary: “Our recommendation is to set your target frame rate to the highest possible value. For most players it will be 60, however your Xbox Series X|S has the capability to play on 120 FPS (refresh rate).”

For more information on playing Halo Infinite with a 120 Hz refresh rate on Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S consoles, review the “How to enable Graphics Quality mode for Halo Infinite” article.

Audio

  • Main: 10

  • Voice: 5

  • Music: 0

  • Menu Music: 0

  • Sound Effects: 10

  • Environmental Effects: 0

  • Hit Detection Effects: 10 CIT commentary: “There is different variance and preferences in audio output because of mix amps and different types of headphones, but we’d recommend starting at this point and adjusting accordingly. The main callouts are sound effects and hit detection to 10 because they will allow you to hear enemy footsteps and other audio cues amidst combat.”

  • Dynamic Range: Dynamic Mode CIT commentary: “We have found dynamic mode to be clearer and more thorough than compressed mode.”

  • Spartan Chatter: Enabled

  • Personal AI Chatter: Enabled CIT commentary: “You should keep these two boxes checked as the spartan chatter can occasionally give you the enemy player’s location. Also, personal AI chatter will deliver small amounts of information, especially around objectives.”

Gameplay

  • Multiplayer Scoreboard Control: Hold/Release CIT commentary: “Changing this to hold/release is preferred because it allows you to open and close your scoreboard faster than setting it to tap (1 input instead of 2). The reason to look at the scoreboard is to confirm information on how many players are dead or alive.”

  • FPS Counter: Enabled

  • Network Statistics: Enabled CIT commentary: “Having both enabled helps verify monitor and internet connections are both configured how you prefer.”

When enabled, the FPS Counter and Network Statistics appear in the top right corner of the screen.

  • Enemy UI Color: Select your preferred color from the following options:

    • Vermilion (Red)
    • Cerise (Purple)
    • Grass (Green)
    • Pineapple (Yellow)

  • Reticle Outline Opacity: 1.0

  • Reticle Outline Thickness: 2.0 CIT commentary: “The increased reticle opacity and thickness portrays a more defined reticle that makes it easier to see lighter-colored outlines in some scenarios.”

  • Show Enemy Names: Enabled

  • Show Friendly Names: Enabled

  • Show Fireteam Names: Enabled

  • Custom Game Player Names: Gamertag CIT commentary: “Showing names based on Gamertags is preferred because it allows for more precise communication when prioritizing kills and assessing information.”

  • Chromatic Aberration: Disabled

  • Bloom: Disabled

  • Parallax: Disabled CIT commentary: “While these User Interface (UI) visual effects give players a heightened sense of immersion, some competitive players may find that adjusting these options will allow them to focus more on their gameplay.”

Accessibility

  • Text Size: Default or Large CIT commentary: “There isn’t a right answer to what is better, it is mainly subjective to the player. Give them both a try and pick which one is best for you.”

  • Blur: 0%

  • Screen Shake: 0%

  • Exposure: 0%

  • Full Screen Effects: 0%

  • Speed Lines: Disabled

  • Sharpening: 60% CIT commentary (same as Video section): “While these settings do give players a heightened sense of immersion, some competitive players may find that adjusting these options will allow them to focus more on their gameplay.”

Safety Features in Halo: Campaign Evolved

Halo: Campaign Evolved includes safety features to help players control their experience and report inappropriate behavior. This article covers the available in-game safety tools, how to verify your safety settings across all supported platforms, and provides additional safety-related resources.

The Spartan Code

The Spartan Code outlines the expected standards of behavior for all Halo players and is a statement of our values. Violations of the Spartan Code may result in enforcement actions.

To view the seven core values in full, read the Spartan Code.

How to Report A Player

You can report players who engage in harassment, unsporting behavior, or other violations of the Spartan Code by following these steps:

Accessing the Report Portal In-game
  • During gameplay, open the pause menu by pressing the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or ESC key (keyboard).
  • Press the X button (XBOX controller), Square button (PlayStation® controller), or X key (keyboard) to open the Report Portal.
  • Scan the QR code using a mobile device, select aka.ms/HaloReport, or press the X button (XBOX controller), Square button (PlayStation® controller), or X key (keyboard).
  • In the newly opened browser, select Submit a report under the Report A Player tile on the Halo Support website. You can also report a player at any time using Halo Support’s Player Report Form.

Any method of accessing the Player Report Form, including in-game or via direct link, will require you to sign in with your Microsoft account if you are not already signed in. Make sure you sign in using the same account you use to play so the report can be submitted correctly.

For more information about filling out the player report form, please see How to Report a Player.

Manage In-Game Safety Settings

Halo: Campaign Evolved includes safety settings that let you manage who can join your group, how you communicate with other players, and how voice chat features are displayed during gameplay.

Change Fireteam Settings

Fireteam settings allow you to control who can join your group. This setting applies to all fireteams you host until you change it again.

  • Open Settings using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Account.
  • Select Fireteam Settings.
    • Select Friends Can Join to allow anyone on your friends list to join your session.
    • Select Invite Only to limit joining to only players you invite.
Change Communication Settings

Halo: Campaign Evolved offers multiple communication options and settings, allowing you to choose how and when you communicate with other players.

Voice Chat
  • Open Settings using the Menu button (XBOX controller), Options button (PlayStation® controller), or F1 (Keyboard).
  • Select Audio.
  • Navigate down to the Voice Chat section.
  • Select Voice Chat Mode.
  • Choose from one of three options:
    • Voice Activated: Your microphone turns on automatically when you speak.
    • Push To Talk: Your microphone turns on only while you hold the assigned button.
    • Disabled: Your microphone is turned off and will not transmit voice audio.
Voice Transcription Widget

Halo: Campaign Evolved includes an optional voice chat widget capable of transcribing voice chat into text and text into speech.

To activate the transcription widget:

  • Open Settings.
  • Select Accessibility.
  • Scroll down to the Voice Chat section.
  • Turn Voice Chat Widget Enabled on or off based on your preference. The widget can be customized in this same accessibility section through settings for text size, global opacity, backing opacity, fade-out timing, and more.

Platform Safety & Family Settings

Platform-level safety settings can restrict communication, multiplayer access, and other features. These settings may override in-game options.

If you’re being blocked from accessing multiplayer and communications features, review your platform’s account and device settings to ensure they are set correctly.

XBOX Consoles/Windows PC/XBOX App

Microsoft and XBOX provide tools that let you manage online safety settings for your account and your family:

  • Microsoft Family management and resources: Your Microsoft Family.
  • XBOX Family management and resources: XBOX Family & Online Safety. Each of these links will take you to a variety of resources for setting screen time limits, managing content restrictions, and more.

Steam

For managing Steam Families, refer to the Steam Families User Guide & FAQ.

This will provide assistance with creating and managing a Steam Family, setting playtime limits, purchase approvals, and more.

PlayStation®5

For setting up a family on PlayStation®, refer to How to Set Up Family Accounts on PlayStation. Once you have set up a family account, refer to How to Set Parental Controls on PlayStation Consoles for setting parental controls like playtime limits, restricting purchases, and more.

Shields in Halo Infinite

Every player in Halo Infinite has a personal shield that provides additional protection during combat. Shields will absorb all damage until they are depleted. If you go without taking damage for about five seconds, your shield energy will replenish.

Your Shield Energy

Your shield energy is shown as a light blue bar at the top of your Heads-Up Display (HUD). Once you have taken damage, your health bar will appear as a smaller, yellow bar below your shield bar. When your shields are fully depleted, a low-pitched warning sound will play, and your shield bar will flash red. If you go without taking damage for about five seconds, a rising tone will play as your shields and health replenish.

The Tutorial in Academy also provides a brief overview of shield health. To access the Tutorial, start in the Play tab on the main menu, navigate down and select Academy. The Tutorial will be the first option on the Academy screen.

Shield Upgrades

In Multiplayer, you can pick up and activate the Overshield Power Equipment piece to gain additional protection during gameplay. The Overshield provides extra protection, but decays over time and does not recharge.

In Campaign, you can gradually upgrade the strength of your Shield Core as you progress through the Campaign. Your shield health can only be upgraded in Campaign. The Shield Core can be upgraded by finding Spartan Core collectibles stashed across Zeta Halo and within mission areas. Use the TacMap menu to view the total number of Spartan Cores in each region or mission. After collecting a Spartan Core, use the Upgrades menu to unlock new abilities for your Equipment or increase your Shield Core strength.

For more information about Equipment upgrades, see our Halo Infinite Weapon, Equipment, and Vehicle Inventory article.

How Weapons Affect Shield Health

Some weapons deal more damage to shields. Plasma weapons, such as the Pulse Carbine and the Plasma Pistol, do more damage to shields, but less damage to health. When walking up to a plasma weapon in-game, the color of the weapon name will be blue.

How to See the Shield Health of Others

In Campaign, opponents with active shields will glow brightly when they take damage. Bosses will have a visible shield/health bar above their heads during each fight. Some enemies will only activate their shields when they know an enemy is nearby. A single shot may be able to significantly damage or even kill an unshielded enemy. Once shields have been depleted, headshots do additional damage.

In Multiplayer, other players’ shields will become visible and glow as they take damage. When the shield breaks, the outline around their body will have a bright flash. Once their shields are broken, sparks of energy will come off their armor.

When you die in Multiplayer, you will see the name of the person who killed you, as well as how much health and shield energy they had when you died.

If a player has an Overshield activated in Multiplayer, their armor will glow white.

Weapons & Vehicles in Halo: Campaign Evolved

WEAPONS & VEHICLES IN HALO: CAMPAIGN EVOLVED

The inventory below is an overview of Halo: Campaign Evolved weapons and vehicles, including their names, roles, and a description from a gameplay perspective. The combat sandbox from the original Halo: Combat Evolved has been expanded with additional weapons and extra vehicle options.

WEAPONS

Weapon

Role

Gameplay Description

Frag Grenade

Area Denial / Explosive

The Frag Grenade will detonate shortly after its first impact, allowing it to be bounced into places direct fire weapons can’t reach.

Magnum Pistol

Precision Sidearm

The Magnum pistol and its integrated scope provide precision at long range, and can eliminate unshielded targets with a single headshot.

SMG

Close-Range Automatic

The SMG is a compact submachine gun. Its high rate of fire and 60-round magazine make it effective in close-quarters combat, but it is less reliable at longer ranges.

Assault Rifle

Mid-Range Automatic

The Assault Rifle (AR) provides sustained automatic fire, with increased accuracy using short, controlled bursts.

Battle Rifle

Precision Burst Rifle

The Battle Rifle (BR) is a precision rifle built for medium range. It fires a 3-round burst, and includes a scope for improved accuracy at long range.

Shotgun

Close-Range Power

The Shotgun is built for high-intensity, close range combat. It can engage targets at longer distances, but with greatly reduced effectiveness.

Sniper Rifle

Long-Range Precision

The Sniper Rifle is built for long-range precision. It includes a scope with multiple magnifications for quick targeting and accurate shots at distance. The rifle fires rounds capable of eliminating most targets with a single headshot.

SPNKr Rocket Launcher

Anti-Vehicle / Heavy Weapon

The Rocket Launcher is a heavy explosive weapon built to engage vehicles and fortified targets. It holds 2 rockets for consecutive shots, features a 2x scope for targeting at long range, and can lock onto air and ground vehicles.

Energy Sword

Melee Power Weapon

The Energy Sword is a melee weapon that can quickly eliminate targets in a single strike, including most shielded ones. At very short distances, it enables a lunge attack that closes the gap.

Plasma Pistol

Shield Disruption

The Plasma Pistol is built for short-range combat and vehicle countering. It supports both semi-automatic and charged firing modes. Standard shots deal consistent damage, while charged shots track targets and can fully deplete most energy shields, and stun vehicles to a stop.

Plasma Rifle

Automatic Energy Weapon

The Plasma Rifle is an energy weapon built for sustained automatic fire at close to medium range. Its rapid fire is effective at overloading energy shields. Controlled bursts help maintain accuracy and prevent overheating.

Needler

Tracking / Burst Damage

The Needler is a projectile weapon built for tracking targets and dealing burst damage at close to medium range. Its projectiles home in on nearby enemies. When multiple projectiles attach to a single target quickly, they trigger a supercombine explosion that can eliminate most unshielded enemies. The projectiles cannot pierce heavy armor like vehicles or hunter plating.

Plasma Grenade

Sticky Explosive

The Plasma Grenade is an adhesive explosive that attaches to living targets. It detonates shortly after impact, releasing a high-damage plasma burst in a small radius. Direct hits can eliminate most targets, including those with active energy shields.

Beam Rifle

Long-Range Energy Precision

The Beam Rifle is an energy weapon built for long-range precision and high single-target damage. It does not require reloading, but rapid use will cause it to overheat. Its scope provides 2 levels of magnification to support accuracy at long range.

Fuel Rod Cannon

Heavy Explosive

The Fuel Rod Cannon is a heavy explosive weapon built fors high-damage, area-of-effect attacks. It fires projectiles that detonate on impact, damaging multiple targets within a blast radius. Projectiles travel in a slow arc, requiring you to lead targets and aim above distant positions.

Needle Rifle

Long-Range Precision

The Needle Rifle fire heavy needler projectiles at high speed. It is most effective at medium to long range. Multiple direct hits in a short period will create a supercombine explosion.

Spiker

Mid-Range Automatic

The Spike Rifle hurl heated shards at a high rate of fire. It is effective at short range, and its bladed barrel deals significant melee damage.

Sentinel Beam

Sterilization

The Sentinel Beam is a Forerunner energy weapon optimized to inhibit Flood growth. The continuous beam is very effective at short to medium range if you can keep it on target.

Brute Plasma Rifle

Automatic Energy Weapon

The Brute Plasma Rifle is an overclocked and unstable version of the Plasma Rifle with a faster rate of fire, issued to Brute shock troops.

The Warthog is built for rapid transport and mobile fire support. Its handling supports quick turns and high-speed movement, all while seating up to four people. The rear machine gun turret provides sustained fire against infantry and lightly armored vehicles.

The Scorpion is a heavily armored tank built for engagements against vehicles, fortifications, and groups of infantry. Its main cannon fires highly explosive rounds, while a secondary operator can control the mounted machine gun for support. The tank can carry up to 4 additional passengers.

The Ghost is a light attack vehicle built for high mobility. It can hover and strafe to avoid incoming fire, provide sustained plasma fire, and includes a temporary speed boost.

The Wraith is a mortar vehicle built for long-range bombardment. It fires plasma projectiles in a high arc, allowing it to hit targets from behind cover. The vehicle is slow, but has heavy armor and deals high area damage.

The Banshee is a mobile aircraft built for both ground attack and aerial combat with automatic plasma cannons and a fuel rod bomb secondary. It can hover, strafe, and boost for movement, but has low durability.

The Shade is a heavy turret built to defend key positions and control chokepoints. It provides sustained fire and partial frontal cover for the operator, but the gunner remains vulnerable to return fire.
